Chapter 1 – String Programming

Q001String

Reverse a string using Java 8 Streams

Reverse characters without using StringBuilder in the Java 8 approach.

Complexity: O(n) time. Java 8 creates an output string of O(n) space; the Java 7 char-array implementation uses O(n) mutable storage.
Sample input / test data
String s = "hello";
Expected output
olleh
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class ReverseStringJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        reverseString();
    }

private static void reverseString() {
    String s = "hello";
    String reversed = IntStream.range(0, s.length())
        .mapToObj(i -> String.valueOf(s.charAt(s.length() - 1 - i)))
        .collect(Collectors.joining());
    System.out.println(reversed);
}
}
Java 7 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class ReverseStringJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        reverseString();
    }

private static void reverseString() {
    String s = "hello";
    char[] chars = s.toCharArray();
    for (int i = 0, j = chars.length - 1; i < j; i++, j--) {
        char temp = chars[i]; chars[i] = chars[j]; chars[j] = temp;
    }
    System.out.println(new String(chars));
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: The Java 8 solution creates indexes from zero to length minus one and reads the source characters in reverse order. The Java 7 solution swaps symmetric characters with two pointers. Both operate on UTF-16 char values, not full grapheme clusters.

Edge cases: Empty and one-character strings return unchanged. Null is outside this example contract and should be rejected before calling the method. Supplementary Unicode characters require code-point-aware reversal.

Interview follow-up: How would you reverse by Unicode code point? How does StringBuilder.reverse() differ from this implementation?

Complexity: O(n) time. Java 8 creates an output string of O(n) space; the Java 7 char-array implementation uses O(n) mutable storage.

Q002String

Reverse each word in a sentence

Reverse each token while retaining word order.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) output/intermediate space.
Sample input / test data
String sentence = "Java   is fun";
Expected output
avaJ si nuf
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class ReverseEachWordInSentenceJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        reverseEachWordInSentence();
    }

private static void reverseEachWordInSentence() {
    String sentence = "Java   is fun";
    String result = sentence.trim().isEmpty() ? "" :
        Arrays.stream(sentence.trim().split("\\s+"))
            .map(word -> new StringBuilder(word).reverse().toString())
            .collect(Collectors.joining(" "));
    System.out.println(result);
}
}
Java 7 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class ReverseEachWordInSentenceJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        reverseEachWordInSentence();
    }

private static void reverseEachWordInSentence() {
    String sentence = "Java   is fun";
    StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
    String trimmed = sentence.trim();
    if (!trimmed.isEmpty()) {
        String[] words = trimmed.split("\\s+");
        for (int i = 0; i < words.length; i++) {
            if (i > 0) result.append(" ");
            result.append(new StringBuilder(words[i]).reverse());
        }
    }
    System.out.println(result.toString());
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Trim the sentence, split on one-or-more whitespace characters, reverse each token, and join tokens with one space. This deliberately normalizes repeated whitespace instead of preserving exact spacing.

Edge cases: Empty or whitespace-only input produces an empty string. Null must be rejected. If preserving original whitespace positions is required, tokenize whitespace and words separately.

Interview follow-up: How would you preserve multiple spaces and tabs exactly? What is the complexity if StringBuilder is used for each word?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) output/intermediate space.

Q003String

Find duplicate characters in a string

Return characters that occur more than once.

Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(k) space for k distinct char values.
Sample input / test data
String s = "apple";
Expected output
[p]
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class FindDuplicateCharactersInStringJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findDuplicateCharactersInString();
    }

private static void findDuplicateCharactersInString() {
    String s = "apple";
    Map<Character, Long> frequency = s.chars().mapToObj(ch -> (char) ch)
        .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Function.identity(), LinkedHashMap::new, Collectors.counting()));
    List<Character> duplicates = frequency.entrySet().stream()
        .filter(e -> e.getValue() > 1).map(Map.Entry::getKey).collect(Collectors.toList());
    System.out.println(duplicates);
}
}
Java 7 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class FindDuplicateCharactersInStringJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findDuplicateCharactersInString();
    }

private static void findDuplicateCharactersInString() {
    String s = "apple";
    Map<Character, Integer> frequency = new LinkedHashMap<Character, Integer>();
    for (char ch : s.toCharArray()) frequency.put(ch, frequency.containsKey(ch) ? frequency.get(ch) + 1 : 1);
    List<Character> duplicates = new ArrayList<Character>();
    for (Map.Entry<Character, Integer> e : frequency.entrySet()) if (e.getValue() > 1) duplicates.add(e.getKey());
    System.out.println(duplicates);
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Build a frequency map in first-appearance order, then collect keys whose count exceeds one. LinkedHashMap makes output ordering deterministic.

Edge cases: No duplicates returns []. Repeated characters appear only once in the result. This version counts UTF-16 char units; use code points for supplementary characters.

Interview follow-up: Can you find duplicates in one pass? What changes if output order is irrelevant?

Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(k) space for k distinct char values.

Q005String

Find the first non-repeated character

Return the earliest character with frequency one.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(k) space.
Sample input / test data
String s = "abac";
Expected output
b
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class FindFirstNonRepeatedCharacterJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findFirstNonRepeatedCharacter();
    }

private static void findFirstNonRepeatedCharacter() {
    String s = "abac";
    Map<Character, Long> counts = s.chars().mapToObj(ch -> (char) ch)
        .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Function.identity(), LinkedHashMap::new, Collectors.counting()));
    Character first = counts.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue() == 1)
        .map(Map.Entry::getKey).findFirst().orElse(null);
    System.out.println(first);
}
}
Java 7 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class FindFirstNonRepeatedCharacterJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findFirstNonRepeatedCharacter();
    }

private static void findFirstNonRepeatedCharacter() {
    String s = "abac";
    Map<Character, Integer> counts = new LinkedHashMap<Character, Integer>();
    for (char ch : s.toCharArray()) counts.put(ch, counts.containsKey(ch) ? counts.get(ch) + 1 : 1);
    Character first = null;
    for (Map.Entry<Character, Integer> e : counts.entrySet()) if (e.getValue() == 1) { first = e.getKey(); break; }
    System.out.println(first);
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Count characters using insertion order, then return the first map entry with count one. This is a two-pass solution: counting first, selection second.

Edge cases: If every character repeats, output is null. An empty string also returns null. Character comparison is case-sensitive.

Interview follow-up: Can this be solved in one pass with an index or queue? What is the trade-off?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(k) space.

Q006String

Find the first repeated character

Return the first character whose second occurrence is encountered.

Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(k) space.
Sample input / test data
String s = "swiss";
Expected output
s
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class FindFirstRepeatedCharacterJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findFirstRepeatedCharacter();
    }

private static void findFirstRepeatedCharacter() {
    String s = "swiss";
    Set<Character> seen = new HashSet<Character>();
    Character repeated = s.chars().mapToObj(ch -> (char) ch)
        .filter(ch -> !seen.add(ch)).findFirst().orElse(null);
    System.out.println(repeated);
}
}
Java 7 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class FindFirstRepeatedCharacterJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findFirstRepeatedCharacter();
    }

private static void findFirstRepeatedCharacter() {
    String s = "swiss";
    Set<Character> seen = new HashSet<Character>();
    Character repeated = null;
    for (char ch : s.toCharArray()) if (!seen.add(ch)) { repeated = ch; break; }
    System.out.println(repeated);
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Scan characters from left to right and maintain a set of previously seen values. The first failed add identifies the character whose second occurrence is encountered earliest. The Java 8 stream is sequential because the set is stateful.

Edge cases: No repeated character returns null. Do not convert this stream to parallel: the mutable seen set and encounter-order requirement make that unsafe.

Interview follow-up: How does this differ from the first character whose total frequency is greater than one? Can LinkedHashSet help?

Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(k) space.

Q007String

Check whether a string is a palindrome

Compare characters from both ends.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
Sample input / test data
String s = "level";
Expected output
true
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class CheckWhetherStringIsPalindromeJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        checkWhetherStringIsPalindrome();
    }

private static void checkWhetherStringIsPalindrome() {
    String s = "level";
    boolean palindrome = IntStream.range(0, s.length() / 2)
        .allMatch(i -> s.charAt(i) == s.charAt(s.length() - 1 - i));
    System.out.println(palindrome);
}
}
Java 7 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class CheckWhetherStringIsPalindromeJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        checkWhetherStringIsPalindrome();
    }

private static void checkWhetherStringIsPalindrome() {
    String s = "level";
    boolean palindrome = true;
    for (int i = 0, j = s.length() - 1; i < j; i++, j--)
        if (s.charAt(i) != s.charAt(j)) { palindrome = false; break; }
    System.out.println(palindrome);
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Only the first half needs checking. Each character at index i must equal the mirrored character at length minus one minus i. allMatch stops on the first mismatch.

Edge cases: Empty and one-character strings are palindromes. This is an exact, case-sensitive comparison; punctuation and case normalization are handled in S018.

Interview follow-up: How do you make this case-insensitive? How does the answer change for Unicode code points?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Q008String

Count vowels and consonants

Count English alphabet vowels and consonants; ignore non-letters.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for the normalized String; a per-character case fold can avoid this copy.
Sample input / test data
String s = "Java 8";
Expected output
vowels=2, consonants=2
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class CountVowelsAndConsonantsJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        countVowelsAndConsonants();
    }

private static void countVowelsAndConsonants() {
    String s = "Java 8".toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT); long vowels = 0, consonants = 0;
    for (char ch : s.toCharArray()) if (ch >= 'a' && ch <= 'z') {
        if ("aeiou".indexOf(ch) >= 0) vowels++; else consonants++;
    }
    System.out.println("vowels=" + vowels + ", consonants=" + consonants);
}
}
Java 7 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class CountVowelsAndConsonantsJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        countVowelsAndConsonants();
    }

private static void countVowelsAndConsonants() {
    String s = "Java 8".toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT); long vowels = 0, consonants = 0;
    for (char ch : s.toCharArray()) if (ch >= 'a' && ch <= 'z') {
        if ("aeiou".indexOf(ch) >= 0) vowels++; else consonants++;
    }
    System.out.println("vowels=" + vowels + ", consonants=" + consonants);
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Normalize case using Locale.ROOT. Inspect only English letters a-z; count a/e/i/o/u as vowels and the remaining English letters as consonants.

Edge cases: Digits, spaces, punctuation and non-ASCII letters are ignored. This is an English-vowel exercise, not a general linguistic classifier.

Interview follow-up: How would you count Unicode letters? How would you include y as a sometimes-vowel?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

    String s = "banana";

Java 7 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class RemoveDuplicateCharactersPreservingOrderJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        removeDuplicateCharactersPreservingOrder();
    }

    String s = "banana";

Explanation and edge cases

Edge cases: Empty input produces an empty string. Comparison is case-sensitive: A and a are different characters.

Q010String

Find maximum occurring character

Return the character with highest frequency; ties use first appearance.

Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(k) space.
Sample input / test data
String s = "hello";
Expected output
l (frequency=2)
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class FindMaximumOccurringCharacterJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findMaximumOccurringCharacter();
    }

private static void findMaximumOccurringCharacter() {
    String s = "hello";
    Map<Character, Long> counts = s.chars().mapToObj(ch -> (char) ch)
        .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Function.identity(), LinkedHashMap::new, Collectors.counting()));
    Character most = counts.entrySet().stream()
        .max((a, b) -> Long.compare(a.getValue(), b.getValue()))
        .map(Map.Entry::getKey).orElse(null);
    System.out.println(most == null ? "null" : most + " (frequency=" + counts.get(most) + ")");
}
}
Java 7 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class FindMaximumOccurringCharacterJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findMaximumOccurringCharacter();
    }

private static void findMaximumOccurringCharacter() {
    String s = "hello";
    Map<Character, Integer> counts = new LinkedHashMap<Character, Integer>();
    for (char ch : s.toCharArray()) counts.put(ch, counts.containsKey(ch) ? counts.get(ch) + 1 : 1);
    Character most = null; int max = 0;
    for (Map.Entry<Character, Integer> e : counts.entrySet()) if (e.getValue() > max) { most = e.getKey(); max = e.getValue(); }
    System.out.println(most == null ? "null" : most + " (frequency=" + max + ")");
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Count in a LinkedHashMap, then select the entry with the largest count. Because ties do not replace the current winner, first appearance wins deterministically. This avoids calling indexOf inside a comparator.

Edge cases: Empty input returns null. If multiple characters share the maximum frequency, the earliest distinct character in the source wins.

Interview follow-up: How would you return all characters tied for maximum frequency? Can a single pass find the winner?

Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(k) space.

Q011String

Find second most frequently occurring character

Rank distinct characters by frequency; ties follow first appearance.

Complexity: O(n + k log k) time and O(k) space for k distinct characters.
Sample input / test data
String s = "aabbbc";
Expected output
a (frequency=2)
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class FindSecondMostFrequentlyOccurringCharacterJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findSecondMostFrequentlyOccurringCharacter();
    }

private static void findSecondMostFrequentlyOccurringCharacter() {
    String s = "aabbbc";
    Map<Character, Long> counts = s.chars().mapToObj(ch -> (char) ch)
        .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Function.identity(), LinkedHashMap::new, Collectors.counting()));
    Character second = counts.entrySet().stream()
        .sorted((a, b) -> Long.compare(b.getValue(), a.getValue()))
        .skip(1).map(Map.Entry::getKey).findFirst().orElse(null);
    System.out.println(second == null ? "null" : second + " (frequency=" + counts.get(second) + ")");
}
}
Java 7 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class FindSecondMostFrequentlyOccurringCharacterJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findSecondMostFrequentlyOccurringCharacter();
    }

private static void findSecondMostFrequentlyOccurringCharacter() {
    String s = "aabbbc";
    Map<Character, Integer> counts = new LinkedHashMap<Character, Integer>();
    for (char ch : s.toCharArray()) counts.put(ch, counts.containsKey(ch) ? counts.get(ch) + 1 : 1);
    List<Character> keys = new ArrayList<Character>(counts.keySet());
    Collections.sort(keys, new Comparator<Character>() {
        public int compare(Character a, Character b) { return Integer.compare(counts.get(b), counts.get(a)); }
    });
    Character second = keys.size() > 1 ? keys.get(1) : null;
    System.out.println(second == null ? "null" : second + " (frequency=" + counts.get(second) + ")");
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Count each distinct character, then sort by descending frequency. The ordered map and stable sort preserve first appearance when frequencies tie. The second entry in the ranking is returned; this is the second-ranked distinct character, not the second occurrence.

Edge cases: Fewer than two distinct characters returns null. For aabbbc the frequencies are b=3, a=2, c=1, so the correct answer is a (not b).

Interview follow-up: How would you return the top K characters? How can a heap reduce sorting cost?

Complexity: O(n + k log k) time and O(k) space for k distinct characters.

Count words and their frequency

Split on whitespace and count normalized tokens.

Complexity: O(n) expected time in total input characters and O(k) space for distinct words.

import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CountWordsAndTheirFrequencyJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        countWordsAndTheirFrequency();
    }

private static void countWordsAndTheirFrequency() {
    String sentence = "java 8 java";
    Map<String, Long> counts = new LinkedHashMap<String, Long>();
    if (!sentence.trim().isEmpty()) {
        counts = Arrays.stream(sentence.trim().split("\\s+"))
            .map(w -> w.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT))
            .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Function.identity(), LinkedHashMap::new, Collectors.counting()));
    }
    System.out.println(counts);
}
}

Q018String

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

true
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class ValidatePalindromeIgnoringPunctuationAndCaseJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        validatePalindromeIgnoringPunctuationAndCase();
    }

private static void validatePalindromeIgnoringPunctuationAndCase() {
    String text = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama";
    int left = 0, right = text.length() - 1;
    boolean palindrome = true;
    while (left < right) {
        while (left < right && !Character.isLetterOrDigit(text.charAt(left))) left++;
        while (left < right && !Character.isLetterOrDigit(text.charAt(right))) right--;
        if (Character.toLowerCase(text.charAt(left)) != Character.toLowerCase(text.charAt(right))) {
            palindrome = false; break;
        }
        left++; right--;
    }
    System.out.println(palindrome);
}
}

    while (left < right) {
        while (left < right && !isVowel(a[left])) left++;
        while (left < right && !isVowel(a[right])) right--;
        char t = a[left]; a[left] = a[right]; a[right] = t;
        left++; right--;
    }
    System.out.println(new String(a));
}
static boolean isVowel(char c) {
    return "aeiouAEIOU".indexOf(c) >= 0;
}
}

import java.util.function.*;

import java.text.*;

public class ConvertSentenceToTitleCaseJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        convertSentenceToTitleCase();
    }

private static void convertSentenceToTitleCase() {
    String sentence = "java   STREAM api";
    StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
    boolean startOfWord = true;
    for (char c : sentence.trim().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).toCharArray()) {
        if (Character.isWhitespace(c)) {
            if (result.length() > 0 && result.charAt(result.length() - 1) != ' ') result.append(' ');
            startOfWord = true;
        } else {
            result.append(startOfWord ? Character.toUpperCase(c) : c);
            startOfWord = false;
        }
    }
    System.out.println(result.toString());
}
}

Q032String

Longest palindromic substring

Return the longest contiguous substring that is a palindrome. When multiple answers have the same maximum length, return the leftmost one.

Complexity: O(n²) time; O(1) auxiliary space (excluding small result arrays).
Sample input / test data
String text = "babad";
Expected output
bab
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class LongestPalindromicSubstringJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        longestPalindromicSubstring();
    }

private static void longestPalindromicSubstring() {
    String text = "babad";
    int bestStart = 0, bestLength = 0;
    for (int center = 0; center < text.length(); center++) {
        int[] odd = expand(text, center, center);
        int[] even = expand(text, center, center + 1);
        if (odd[1] > bestLength) { bestStart = odd[0]; bestLength = odd[1]; }
        if (even[1] > bestLength) { bestStart = even[0]; bestLength = even[1]; }
    }
    System.out.println(text.substring(bestStart, bestStart + bestLength));
}
static int[] expand(String s, int left, int right) {
    while (left >= 0 && right < s.length() && s.charAt(left) == s.charAt(right)) { left--; right++; }
    return new int[] {left + 1, right - left - 1};
}
}

        if (right - left + 1 > bestLength) { bestStart = left; bestLength = right - left + 1; }
    }

        best = Math.max(best, right - left + 1);
    }

    }

private static void findSubstringsFormedByConcatenatingAllGivenWords() {
    String text = "barfoothefoobarman"; String[] words = {"foo", "bar"};
    List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    if (words.length == 0) { System.out.println(result); return; }
    if (words[0] == null || words[0].length() == 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("words must be non-empty");
    int wordLength = words[0].length();
    for (String word : words) if (word == null || word.length() != wordLength) throw new IllegalArgumentException("all words must have equal non-zero length");
    long totalLengthLong = (long) wordLength * words.length;
    if (totalLengthLong > text.length()) { System.out.println(result); return; }
    int totalLength = (int) totalLengthLong;
    Map<String, Integer> need = new HashMap<String, Integer>();
    for (String word : words) need.put(word, need.containsKey(word) ? need.get(word) + 1 : 1);
    for (int offset = 0; offset < wordLength; offset++) {
        int left = offset, used = 0; Map<String, Integer> window = new HashMap<String, Integer>();
        for (int right = offset; right + wordLength <= text.length(); right += wordLength) {
            String word = text.substring(right, right + wordLength);
            if (!need.containsKey(word)) { window.clear(); used = 0; left = right + wordLength; continue; }
            window.put(word, window.containsKey(word) ? window.get(word) + 1 : 1); used++;
            while (window.get(word) > need.get(word)) { String drop = text.substring(left, left + wordLength); window.put(drop, window.get(drop) - 1); used--; left += wordLength; }
            if (used == words.length) { result.add(left); String drop = text.substring(left, left + wordLength); window.put(drop, window.get(drop) - 1); used--; left += wordLength; }
        }
    }
    Collections.sort(result); System.out.println(result);
}
}

10

import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;

    public static void main(String[] args) {

    }

private static void implementKMPPatternSearching() {
    String text = "ababcabcabababd", pattern = "ababd";
    System.out.println(kmpIndexOf(text, pattern));
}
static int kmpIndexOf(String text, String pattern) {
    if (pattern.length() == 0) return 0;
    int[] lps = buildLps(pattern);
    int i = 0, j = 0;
    while (i < text.length()) {
        if (text.charAt(i) == pattern.charAt(j)) { i++; j++; if (j == pattern.length()) return i - j; }
        else if (j > 0) j = lps[j - 1];
        else i++;
    }
    return -1;
}
static int[] buildLps(String p) {
    int[] lps = new int[p.length()]; int len = 0, i = 1;
    while (i < p.length()) {
        if (p.charAt(i) == p.charAt(len)) lps[i++] = ++len;
        else if (len > 0) len = lps[len - 1];
        else lps[i++] = 0;
    }
    return lps;
}
}

Q041String

Implement Rabin–Karp pattern searching

Find all occurrences of a pattern using a rolling hash, verifying characters when hashes match to avoid accepting collisions.

Complexity: Expected O(n + m + r·m) time; O(1) auxiliary space excluding result, where r is the number of hash matches verified.
Sample input / test data
String text = "GEEKS FOR GEEKS";
String pattern = "GEEK";
Expected output
[0, 10]
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class ImplementRabinKarpPatternSearchingJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        implementRabinKarpPatternSearching();
    }

private static void implementRabinKarpPatternSearching() {
    String text = "GEEKS FOR GEEKS", pattern = "GEEK";
    System.out.println(rabinKarp(text, pattern));
}
static List<Integer> rabinKarp(String text, String pattern) {
    List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    int n = text.length(), m = pattern.length();
    if (m == 0 || m > n) return result;
    long mod = 1000000007L, base = 256L, high = 1, patternHash = 0, windowHash = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < m; i++) high = (high * base) % mod;
    for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
        patternHash = (patternHash * base + pattern.charAt(i)) % mod;
        windowHash = (windowHash * base + text.charAt(i)) % mod;
    }
    for (int start = 0; start <= n - m; start++) {
        if (patternHash == windowHash && text.regionMatches(start, pattern, 0, m)) result.add(start);
        if (start < n - m) {
            windowHash = (windowHash - text.charAt(start) * high % mod + mod) % mod;
            windowHash = (windowHash * base + text.charAt(start + m)) % mod;
        }
    }
    return result;
}
}

public class ImplementRabinKarpPatternSearchingJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        implementRabinKarpPatternSearching();
    }

private static void implementRabinKarpPatternSearching() {
    String text = "GEEKS FOR GEEKS", pattern = "GEEK";
    System.out.println(rabinKarp(text, pattern));
}
static List<Integer> rabinKarp(String text, String pattern) {
    List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    int n = text.length(), m = pattern.length();
    if (m == 0 || m > n) return result;
    long mod = 1000000007L, base = 256L, high = 1, patternHash = 0, windowHash = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < m; i++) high = (high * base) % mod;
    for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
        patternHash = (patternHash * base + pattern.charAt(i)) % mod;
        windowHash = (windowHash * base + text.charAt(i)) % mod;
    }
    for (int start = 0; start <= n - m; start++) {
        if (patternHash == windowHash && text.regionMatches(start, pattern, 0, m)) result.add(start);
        if (start < n - m) {
            windowHash = (windowHash - text.charAt(start) * high % mod + mod) % mod;
            windowHash = (windowHash * base + text.charAt(start + m)) % mod;
        }
    }
    return result;
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Hash the pattern and the first text window. Slide the hash in constant time by removing the outgoing character and adding the incoming one. Verify a matching hash character-by-character.

Edge cases: Empty patterns return no matches by this problem definition. Hash collisions are possible, so verification is required. Uses UTF-16 char values.

Interview follow-up: How would you extend this to two-dimensional pattern matching or multiple patterns?

Complexity: Expected O(n + m + r·m) time; O(1) auxiliary space excluding result, where r is the number of hash matches verified.

    String text = "level";

    while (i < text.length()) {

        else if (len > 0) len = lps[len - 1];
        else lps[i++] = 0;
    }
    System.out.println(text.substring(0, lps[text.length() - 1]));
}
}

Build the shortest palindrome by adding characters at the beginning

Java 8 complete runnable program

import java.util.stream.*;

public class BuildShortestPalindromeByAddingCharactersAtBeginningJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        buildShortestPalindromeByAddingCharactersAtBeginning();
    }

private static void buildShortestPalindromeByAddingCharactersAtBeginning() {
    String text = "aacecaaa";
    int n = text.length();
    int[] sequence = new int[2 * n + 1];
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) sequence[i] = text.charAt(i);
    sequence[n] = -1; // no char value can equal this separator
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) sequence[n + 1 + i] = text.charAt(n - 1 - i);
    int[] lps = new int[sequence.length]; int len = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < sequence.length; ) {
        if (sequence[i] == sequence[len]) lps[i++] = ++len;
        else if (len > 0) len = lps[len - 1];
        else lps[i++] = 0;
    }
    String reversed = new StringBuilder(text).reverse().toString();
    int prefixPalindromeLength = lps[sequence.length - 1];
    System.out.println(reversed.substring(0, n - prefixPalindromeLength) + text);
}
}

private static void findRepeatedDNASequencesOfLengthTen() {
    String dna = "AAAAACCCCCAAAAACCCCCCAAAAAGGGTTT";
    Set<String> seen = new HashSet<String>(); Set<String> repeated = new LinkedHashSet<String>();
    for (int i = 0; i < dna.length(); i++) if ("ACGT".indexOf(dna.charAt(i)) < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("DNA must contain A, C, G or T");
    for (int i = 0; i + 10 <= dna.length(); i++) { String part = dna.substring(i, i + 10); if (!seen.add(part)) repeated.add(part); }
    System.out.println(new ArrayList<String>(repeated));
}
}

Q046String

Longest common substring

Find the longest contiguous substring shared by two strings and return that substring. If there is a tie, retain the first maximum found by row-major scanning.

Complexity: O(n × m) time; O(n × m) space.
Sample input / test data
String first = "ABABC";
String second = "BABCA";
Expected output
BABC
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class LongestCommonSubstringJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        longestCommonSubstring();
    }

private static void longestCommonSubstring() {
    String first = "ABABC", second = "BABCA";
    int[][] dp = new int[first.length() + 1][second.length() + 1];
    int best = 0, end = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i <= first.length(); i++) {
        for (int j = 1; j <= second.length(); j++) {
            if (first.charAt(i - 1) == second.charAt(j - 1)) {
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1;
                if (dp[i][j] > best) { best = dp[i][j]; end = i; }
            }
        }
    }
    System.out.println(first.substring(end - best, end));
}
}

Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: For matching characters, extend the common suffix by one from the diagonal cell. A mismatch resets the cell to zero because the substring must be contiguous.

Edge cases: If there is no common character, return empty. Longest common substring is different from longest common subsequence because gaps are not allowed.

Interview follow-up: How can rolling rows reduce the DP space to O(min(n,m))?

Complexity: O(n × m) time; O(n × m) space.

Longest common subsequence and reconstruct the sequence

Return one longest sequence that appears in both strings in the same relative order, but not necessarily contiguously.

Complexity: O(n × m) time and O(n × m) space.
Sample input / test data
String first = "abcde";
String second = "ace";
Expected output
length=3, sequence=ace
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class LongestCommonSubsequenceAndReconstructSequenceJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        longestCommonSubsequenceAndReconstructSequence();
    }

private static void longestCommonSubsequenceAndReconstructSequence() {
    String first = "abcde", second = "ace";
    int[][] dp = new int[first.length() + 1][second.length() + 1];
    for (int i = 1; i <= first.length(); i++) for (int j = 1; j <= second.length(); j++) {
        if (first.charAt(i - 1) == second.charAt(j - 1)) dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1;
        else dp[i][j] = Math.max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]);
    }
    StringBuilder sequence = new StringBuilder(); int i = first.length(), j = second.length();
    while (i > 0 && j > 0) {
        if (first.charAt(i - 1) == second.charAt(j - 1)) { sequence.append(first.charAt(i - 1)); i--; j--; }
        else if (dp[i - 1][j] >= dp[i][j - 1]) i--; else j--;
    }
    sequence.reverse();
    System.out.println("length=" + dp[first.length()][second.length()] + ", sequence=" + sequence);
}
}

Q048String

Calculate edit distance (Levenshtein distance)

Find the minimum number of insertions, deletions and substitutions needed to transform one string into another.

Complexity: O(n × m) time; O(n × m) space.
Sample input / test data
String source = "horse";
String target = "ros";
Expected output
3
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class CalculateEditDistanceJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        calculateEditDistance();
    }

private static void calculateEditDistance() {
    String source = "horse", target = "ros";
    int[][] dp = new int[source.length() + 1][target.length() + 1];
    for (int i = 0; i <= source.length(); i++) dp[i][0] = i;
    for (int j = 0; j <= target.length(); j++) dp[0][j] = j;
    for (int i = 1; i <= source.length(); i++) for (int j = 1; j <= target.length(); j++) {
        int cost = source.charAt(i - 1) == target.charAt(j - 1) ? 0 : 1;
        dp[i][j] = Math.min(Math.min(dp[i - 1][j] + 1, dp[i][j - 1] + 1), dp[i - 1][j - 1] + cost);
    }
    System.out.println(dp[source.length()][target.length()]);
}
}

Edge cases: Identical strings have distance zero. Empty-to-nonempty distance is the other string length. The model assigns equal cost to each edit operation.

Interview follow-up: How would you return the actual edit sequence? How can rolling rows reduce memory?

Complexity: O(n × m) time; O(n × m) space.

Q050String

Check whether a string is an interleaving of two strings

Check whether the target can be formed by interleaving all characters of two source strings while preserving the order within each source.

Complexity: O(n × m) time; O(n × m) space.
Sample input / test data
String first = "aabcc";
String second = "dbbca";
String target = "aadbbcbcac";
Expected output
true
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class CheckWhetherStringIsInterleavingOfTwoStringsJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        checkWhetherStringIsInterleavingOfTwoStrings();
    }

private static void checkWhetherStringIsInterleavingOfTwoStrings() {
    String first = "aabcc", second = "dbbca", target = "aadbbcbcac";
    if (first.length() + second.length() != target.length()) { System.out.println(false); return; }
    boolean[][] dp = new boolean[first.length() + 1][second.length() + 1]; dp[0][0] = true;
    for (int i = 0; i <= first.length(); i++) for (int j = 0; j <= second.length(); j++) {
        int k = i + j - 1;
        if (i > 0 && first.charAt(i - 1) == target.charAt(k)) dp[i][j] |= dp[i - 1][j];
        if (j > 0 && second.charAt(j - 1) == target.charAt(k)) dp[i][j] |= dp[i][j - 1];
    }
    System.out.println(dp[first.length()][second.length()]);
}
}

public class BuildShortestCommonSupersequenceJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        buildShortestCommonSupersequence();
    }

private static void buildShortestCommonSupersequence() {
    String first = "abac", second = "cab";
    int[][] lcs = new int[first.length() + 1][second.length() + 1];
    for (int i = 1; i <= first.length(); i++) for (int j = 1; j <= second.length(); j++)
        lcs[i][j] = first.charAt(i - 1) == second.charAt(j - 1)
            ? lcs[i - 1][j - 1] + 1 : Math.max(lcs[i - 1][j], lcs[i][j - 1]);
    StringBuilder reversed = new StringBuilder(); int i = first.length(), j = second.length();
    while (i > 0 && j > 0) {
        if (first.charAt(i - 1) == second.charAt(j - 1)) { reversed.append(first.charAt(i - 1)); i--; j--; }
        else if (lcs[i - 1][j] >= lcs[i][j - 1]) reversed.append(first.charAt(--i));
        else reversed.append(second.charAt(--j));
    }
    while (i > 0) reversed.append(first.charAt(--i));
    while (j > 0) reversed.append(second.charAt(--j));
    System.out.println(reversed.reverse().toString());
}
}

Q053String

Implement atoi string-to-integer conversion

Parse a signed decimal integer after leading whitespace, stop at the first non-digit, and clamp overflow to the 32-bit signed integer range.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space.
Sample input / test data
String text = " -42xyz";
Expected output
-42
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class ImplementAtoiStringToIntegerConversionJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        implementAtoiStringToIntegerConversion();
    }

private static void implementAtoiStringToIntegerConversion() {
    String text = " -42xyz";
    int i = 0, n = text.length();
    while (i < n && Character.isWhitespace(text.charAt(i))) i++;
    int sign = 1;
    if (i < n && (text.charAt(i) == '+' || text.charAt(i) == '-')) sign = text.charAt(i++) == '-' ? -1 : 1;
    long limit = sign == 1 ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : -(long) Integer.MIN_VALUE;
    long value = 0;
    while (i < n && text.charAt(i) >= '0' && text.charAt(i) <= '9') {
        int digit = text.charAt(i++) - '0';
        if (value > (limit - digit) / 10) { value = limit; break; }
        value = value * 10 + digit;
    }
    long signed = sign * value;
    if (signed > Integer.MAX_VALUE) signed = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
    if (signed < Integer.MIN_VALUE) signed = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
    System.out.println((int) signed);
}
}

    String roman = "MCMXCIV";
    Map<Character, Integer> value = new HashMap<Character, Integer>();

        total += current < next ? -current : current;
    }

}
}

        if (Character.isDigit(c)) { number = number * 10 + (c - '0'); readingNumber = true; if (number > Integer.MAX_VALUE) throw new IllegalArgumentException("repeat count too large"); }
        else if (c == '[') { if (!readingNumber) throw new IllegalArgumentException("missing repeat count"); counts.push((int) number); prefixes.push(current); number = 0; readingNumber = false; current = new StringBuilder(); }
        else if (c == ']') { if (counts.isEmpty() || readingNumber) throw new IllegalArgumentException("malformed encoding"); int repeat = counts.pop(); StringBuilder parent = prefixes.pop(); for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++) parent.append(current); current = parent; }
        else { if (readingNumber) throw new IllegalArgumentException("count must be followed by '['"); current.append(c); }
    }
    if (!counts.isEmpty() || readingNumber) throw new IllegalArgumentException("unclosed encoding");
    System.out.println(current.toString());
}
}

Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Use one stack for repeat counts and one stack for the string prefix preceding each opening bracket. When a closing bracket is found, repeat the current segment and append it to the saved prefix.

Edge cases: Input must be syntactically valid, with matching brackets and non-negative repeat counts. Very large repeat counts can cause memory exhaustion; production code should enforce output-size limits.

    }

private static void generateCountAndSaySequence() {
    int n = 5;
    if (n <= 0) { System.out.println(""); return; }
    String term = "1";
    for (int step = 2; step <= n; step++) {
        StringBuilder next = new StringBuilder(); int i = 0;
        while (i < term.length()) {

            while (i < term.length() && term.charAt(i) == digit) { count++; i++; }
            next.append(count).append(digit);
        }

    }
    System.out.println(term);
}
}

Q062String

Convert a string into Zigzag form

Write characters down and diagonally across a specified number of rows, then read row by row.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(n) space.
Sample input / test data
String text = "PAYPALISHIRING";
int rows = 3;
Expected output
PAHNAPLSIIGYIR
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class ConvertStringIntoZigzagFormJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        convertStringIntoZigzagForm();
    }

private static void convertStringIntoZigzagForm() {
    String text = "PAYPALISHIRING"; int rows = 3;
    if (rows <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("rows must be positive");
    if (rows == 1 || rows >= text.length()) { System.out.println(text); return; }
    List<StringBuilder> lines = new ArrayList<StringBuilder>();
    for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) lines.add(new StringBuilder());
    int row = 0, direction = 1;
    for (char c : text.toCharArray()) {
        lines.get(row).append(c);
        if (row == 0) direction = 1;
        else if (row == rows - 1) direction = -1;
        row += direction;
    }
    StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
    for (StringBuilder line : lines) result.append(line);
    System.out.println(result.toString());
}
}

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        restoreAllValidIPAddresses();
    }

private static void restoreAllValidIPAddresses() {
    String digits = "25525511135";
    List<String> result = new ArrayList<String>();
    restoreIp(digits, 0, 0, new ArrayList<String>(), result);
    System.out.println(result);

static void restoreIp(String s, int index, int parts, List<String> path, List<String> result) {
    if (parts == 4) {
        if (index == s.length()) result.add(joinParts(path));
        return;
    }
    for (int len = 1; len <= 3 && index + len <= s.length(); len++) {
        String part = s.substring(index, index + len);
        if (part.length() > 1 && part.charAt(0) == '0') break;
        int value = Integer.parseInt(part);
        if (value > 255) break;
        path.add(part); restoreIp(s, index + len, parts + 1, path, result); path.remove(path.size() - 1);
    }
}
static String joinParts(List<String> parts) {
    StringBuilder b = new StringBuilder();
    for (int i = 0; i < parts.size(); i++) { if (i > 0) b.append('.'); b.append(parts.get(i)); }
    return b.toString();
}
}

Sample input / test data

1
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class EvaluateBasicArithmeticExpressionParenthesesJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        evaluateBasicArithmeticExpressionParentheses();
    }

private static void evaluateBasicArithmeticExpressionParentheses() {
    String expression = "1-(2-3)+(4-5)";
    Deque<Integer> signs = new ArrayDeque<Integer>(); signs.push(1);
    int sign = 1, number = 0, result = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < expression.length(); i++) {
        char c = expression.charAt(i);
        if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') number = number * 10 + c - '0';
        else if (c == '+' || c == '-') {
            result += sign * number; number = 0;
            sign = (c == '+' ? 1 : -1) * signs.peek();
        } else if (c == '(') signs.push(sign);
        else if (c == ')') { result += sign * number; number = 0; signs.pop(); sign = signs.peek(); }
    }
    result += sign * number;
    System.out.println(result);
}
}

Complexity: O(n) time and O(d) space for maximum parenthesis depth.

Q065String

Find the longest duplicate substring

Return the longest substring that occurs at least twice in the input. Overlapping occurrences are allowed.

Complexity: Worst-case comparison work can reach O(n² log n); auxiliary sorting/index storage is O(n).
Sample input / test data
String text = "banana";
Expected output
ana
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class FindLongestDuplicateSubstringJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findLongestDuplicateSubstring();
    }

private static void findLongestDuplicateSubstring() {
    String text = "banana";
    Integer[] suffixes = new Integer[text.length()];
    for (int i = 0; i < text.length(); i++) suffixes[i] = i;
    Arrays.sort(suffixes, new Comparator<Integer>() {
        public int compare(Integer a, Integer b) { return text.substring(a).compareTo(text.substring(b)); }
    });
    String best = "";
    for (int i = 1; i < suffixes.length; i++) {
        int common = commonPrefix(text, suffixes[i - 1], suffixes[i]);
        if (common > best.length()) best = text.substring(suffixes[i], suffixes[i] + common);
    }
    System.out.println(best);
}
static int commonPrefix(String s, int i, int j) {
    int length = 0;
    while (i + length < s.length() && j + length < s.length()
            && s.charAt(i + length) == s.charAt(j + length)) length++;
    return length;
}
}

Implement a Trie with insert, search and prefix lookup

Implement a prefix tree supporting word insertion, exact-word search and prefix search using lowercase English letters.

Complexity: O(L) expected time per operation and O(total inserted characters) space.
Sample input / test data
Trie trie = new Trie();
trie.insert("apple");
// query: search("apple"), search("app"), startsWith("app")
Expected output
search(apple)=true
search(app)=false
startsWith(app)=true
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class ImplementTrieInsertSearchAndPrefixLookupJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        implementTrieInsertSearchAndPrefixLookup();
    }

static class TrieNode {
    Map<Character, TrieNode> children = new HashMap<Character, TrieNode>();
    boolean isWord;
}
static class Trie {
    private final TrieNode root = new TrieNode();
    void insert(String word) {
        if (word == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("word must not be null");
        TrieNode node = root;
        for (char c : word.toCharArray()) {
            if (!node.children.containsKey(c)) node.children.put(c, new TrieNode());
            node = node.children.get(c);
        }
        node.isWord = true;
    }
    boolean search(String word) {
        TrieNode node = find(word); return node != null && node.isWord;
    }
    boolean startsWith(String prefix) { return find(prefix) != null; }
    private TrieNode find(String text) {
        if (text == null) return null;
        TrieNode node = root;
        for (char c : text.toCharArray()) {
            node = node.children.get(c);
            if (node == null) return null;
        }
        return node;
    }
}
private static void implementTrieInsertSearchAndPrefixLookup() {
    Trie trie = new Trie(); trie.insert("apple");
    System.out.println("search(apple)=" + trie.search("apple"));
    System.out.println("search(app)=" + trie.search("app"));
    System.out.println("startsWith(app)=" + trie.startsWith("app"));
}
}

Q067String

Wildcard pattern matching with ? and *

Determine whether a pattern matches the entire input string. ? matches one character; * matches zero or more characters.

Complexity: O(n × m) time and O(n × m) space.
Sample input / test data
String text = "adceb";
String pattern = "*a*b";
Expected output
true
Java 8 complete runnable program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;
import java.text.*;

public class WildcardPatternMatchingAndJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        wildcardPatternMatchingAnd();
    }

private static void wildcardPatternMatchingAnd() {
    String text = "adceb", pattern = "*a*b";
    boolean[][] dp = new boolean[text.length() + 1][pattern.length() + 1];
    dp[0][0] = true;
    for (int j = 1; j <= pattern.length(); j++)
        if (pattern.charAt(j - 1) == '*') dp[0][j] = dp[0][j - 1];
    for (int i = 1; i <= text.length(); i++) for (int j = 1; j <= pattern.length(); j++) {
        char p = pattern.charAt(j - 1);
        if (p == '*') dp[i][j] = dp[i][j - 1] || dp[i - 1][j];
        else if (p == '?' || p == text.charAt(i - 1)) dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1];
    }
    System.out.println(dp[text.length()][pattern.length()]);
}
}

        if (pattern.charAt(j - 1) == '*') dp[0][j] = dp[0][j - 1];
    for (int i = 1; i <= text.length(); i++) for (int j = 1; j <= pattern.length(); j++) {
        char p = pattern.charAt(j - 1);
        if (p == '*') dp[i][j] = dp[i][j - 1] || dp[i - 1][j];
        else if (p == '?' || p == text.charAt(i - 1)) dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1];
    }
    System.out.println(dp[text.length()][pattern.length()]);
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Dynamic programming state dp[i][j] means the first i text characters match the first j pattern characters. A star can match zero characters (left cell) or one more text character (above cell); question mark matches any single char.

Edge cases: Empty text matches only patterns consisting entirely of stars. Null values are rejected. The full table uses O(nm) memory; a rolling row can reduce it to O(m).

Interview follow-up: How would you optimize memory to O(pattern length)? What is the difference between wildcard and regular-expression matching?

Complexity: O(n × m) time and O(n × m) space.

    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3, 4);
    if (nums.contains(null)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null elements are not supported");
    Map<Boolean, List<Integer>> parts = nums.stream().collect(Collectors.partitioningBy(n -> n % 2 == 0));
    System.out.println("even=" + parts.get(true) + ", odd=" + parts.get(false));
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;

public class SeparateEvenAndOddNumbersJava7 {

    }

private static void separateEvenAndOddNumbers() {

    List<Integer> even = new ArrayList<Integer>(), odd = new ArrayList<Integer>();

Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Partition each integer by the predicate n % 2 == 0. partitioningBy always creates both true and false buckets. The Java 7 version fills two lists in one pass.

Q069List<Integer>

Find duplicate elements in a list

Solve the problem with a clear input contract and deterministic output.

Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(k) space for k distinct values.
Sample input / test data
List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3);
Expected output
[2, 3]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindDuplicateElementsInListJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findDuplicateElementsInList();
    }

private static void findDuplicateElementsInList() {
    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3);
    if (nums.contains(null)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null elements are not supported");
    Map<Integer, Long> counts = nums.stream().collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Function.identity(), LinkedHashMap::new, Collectors.counting()));
    List<Integer> duplicates = counts.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue() > 1)
        .map(Map.Entry::getKey).collect(Collectors.toList());
    System.out.println(duplicates);
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindDuplicateElementsInListJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findDuplicateElementsInList();
    }

private static void findDuplicateElementsInList() {
    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3);
    if (nums.contains(null)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null elements are not supported");
    Map<Integer, Integer> counts = new LinkedHashMap<Integer, Integer>();
    for (Integer n : nums) { if (n == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null element"); counts.put(n, counts.containsKey(n) ? counts.get(n) + 1 : 1); }
    List<Integer> duplicates = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    for (Map.Entry<Integer, Integer> e : counts.entrySet()) if (e.getValue() > 1) duplicates.add(e.getKey());
    System.out.println(duplicates);
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Count occurrences with groupingBy and counting, then retain keys with a count greater than one. Unlike a filter with an external seen set, this solution has no stateful side effects inside the stream pipeline.

Edge cases: Each duplicated value appears once in first-appearance order. Null values are rejected. This reports duplicate values, not every repeated occurrence.

Interview follow-up: Why is mutating a HashSet inside filter a problem for parallel streams? How would you return counts as well?

Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(k) space for k distinct values.

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;

public class FindSecondHighestDistinctNumberJava8 {

    }

private static void findSecondHighestDistinctNumber() {
    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(10, 5, 10, 8, 8, 3);
    if (nums.contains(null)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null elements are not supported");
    Integer value = nums.stream().distinct().sorted(Comparator.reverseOrder()).skip(1).findFirst().orElse(null);
    System.out.println("second-highest=" + value);
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;

public class FindSecondHighestDistinctNumberJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {

    }

private static void findSecondHighestDistinctNumber() {
    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(10, 5, 10, 8, 8, 3);
    Set<Integer> distinct = new TreeSet<Integer>(Collections.reverseOrder());
    for (Integer n : nums) { if (n == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null element"); distinct.add(n); }

Q073List<Integer>

Find maximum and minimum values

Solve the problem with a clear input contract and deterministic output.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
Sample input / test data

Expected output
min=-1, max=9
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindMaximumAndMinimumValuesJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findMaximumAndMinimumValues();
    }

private static void findMaximumAndMinimumValues() {
    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(4, 2, 9, -1, 7);
    if (nums.isEmpty()) { System.out.println("min=empty, max=empty"); return; }
    if (nums.contains(null)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null elements are not supported");
    IntSummaryStatistics stats = nums.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).summaryStatistics();
    System.out.println("min=" + stats.getMin() + ", max=" + stats.getMax());
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindMaximumAndMinimumValuesJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findMaximumAndMinimumValues();
    }

private static void findMaximumAndMinimumValues() {
    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(4, 2, 9, -1, 7);
    if (nums.isEmpty()) { System.out.println("min=empty, max=empty"); return; }
    int min = Integer.MAX_VALUE, max = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
    for (Integer n : nums) { if (n == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null element"); if (n < min) min = n; if (n > max) max = n; }
    System.out.println("min=" + min + ", max=" + max);
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: IntSummaryStatistics computes count, sum, minimum, maximum and average in one traversal. The empty check is explicit so Java 8 and Java 7 versions share the same contract.

Edge cases: Empty input prints empty rather than misleading numeric sentinels. Null elements are rejected. Integer.MIN_VALUE and MAX_VALUE are handled correctly.

Interview follow-up: How do you compute min and max in one pass without summary statistics? What is the benefit of primitive streams?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Q074List<Integer>

Calculate sum and average

Solve the problem with a clear input contract and deterministic output.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(10, 20, 30);
Expected output
sum=60, average=20.0
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class CalculateSumAndAverageJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        calculateSumAndAverage();
    }

private static void calculateSumAndAverage() {
    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(10, 20, 30);
    if (nums.isEmpty()) { System.out.println("sum=0, average=undefined"); return; }
    if (nums.contains(null)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null elements are not supported");
    IntSummaryStatistics stats = nums.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).summaryStatistics();
    System.out.println("sum=" + stats.getSum() + ", average=" + stats.getAverage());
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class CalculateSumAndAverageJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        calculateSumAndAverage();
    }

private static void calculateSumAndAverage() {
    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(10, 20, 30);
    if (nums.isEmpty()) { System.out.println("sum=0, average=undefined"); return; }
    long sum = 0; for (Integer n : nums) { if (n == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null element"); sum += n; }

}
Explanation and edge cases

Interview follow-up: Why use mapToInt instead of map? How would you safely sum arbitrary BigInteger values?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

import java.util.*;

    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6);
    if (nums.contains(null)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null elements are not supported");
    OptionalDouble average = nums.stream().filter(n -> n % 2 == 0).mapToInt(Integer::intValue).average();
    System.out.println(average.isPresent() ? "average-even=" + average.getAsDouble() : "average-even=undefined");

}

import java.util.*;

Q076List<Integer>

Find common elements between two lists

Solve the problem with a clear input contract and deterministic output.

Complexity: O(n + m) expected time and O(m + k) space.
Sample input / test data
List<Integer> first = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2, 3, 4);
List<Integer> second = Arrays.asList(2, 4, 6);
Expected output
[2, 4]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindCommonElementsBetweenTwoListsJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findCommonElementsBetweenTwoLists();
    }

private static void findCommonElementsBetweenTwoLists() {
    List<Integer> first = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2, 3, 4);
    List<Integer> second = Arrays.asList(2, 4, 6);
    Set<Integer> lookup = new HashSet<Integer>(second);
    List<Integer> common = first.stream().filter(lookup::contains).distinct().collect(Collectors.toList());
    System.out.println(common);
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindCommonElementsBetweenTwoListsJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findCommonElementsBetweenTwoLists();
    }

private static void findCommonElementsBetweenTwoLists() {
    List<Integer> first = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2, 3, 4);
    List<Integer> second = Arrays.asList(2, 4, 6);
    Set<Integer> lookup = new HashSet<Integer>(second), emitted = new HashSet<Integer>();
    List<Integer> common = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    for (Integer n : first) if (lookup.contains(n) && emitted.add(n)) common.add(n);
    System.out.println(common);
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Build a HashSet for fast membership checks in the second list. Traverse the first list and emit matching values once; this defines set-intersection semantics and preserves first-list order.

Edge cases: Duplicate values are returned once. If multiset intersection is required, each occurrence count must be tracked instead. Null is permitted by HashSet but should be explicitly included in the problem contract.

Interview follow-up: How would you compute multiset intersection? What is the expected complexity of HashSet.contains?

Complexity: O(n + m) expected time and O(m + k) space.

List<Integer> first = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2, 3, 4);

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindElementsInFirstListButNotSecondJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findElementsInFirstListButNotSecond();
    }

private static void findElementsInFirstListButNotSecond() {
    List<Integer> first = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2, 3, 4);
    List<Integer> second = Arrays.asList(2, 4);
    Set<Integer> excluded = new HashSet<Integer>(second);
    Set<Integer> difference = first.stream().filter(n -> !excluded.contains(n))
        .collect(Collectors.toCollection(LinkedHashSet::new));
    System.out.println(new ArrayList<Integer>(difference));

}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

    List<Integer> first = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2, 3, 4);

    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(10, 4, 7, 10, 8, 9);
    if (nums.contains(null)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("null elements are not supported");
    List<Integer> top = nums.stream().distinct().sorted(Comparator.reverseOrder()).limit(3).collect(Collectors.toList());
    System.out.println(top);
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindTopThreeLargestDistinctNumbersJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findTopThreeLargestDistinctNumbers();
    }

private static void findTopThreeLargestDistinctNumbers() {
    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(10, 4, 7, 10, 8, 9);
    Set<Integer> sorted = new TreeSet<Integer>(Collections.reverseOrder()); sorted.addAll(nums);
    List<Integer> top = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    for (Integer n : sorted) { if (top.size() == 3) break; top.add(n); }
    System.out.println(top);
}
}
Explanation and edge cases

Approach: Distinct removes repeated values, descending sort ranks them, and limit(3) selects at most three values. Fewer than three distinct values returns all available values.

Edge cases: Nulls are rejected. This sorts all distinct values; for very large lists and small K, a size-K heap can reduce time to O(n log K).

Interview follow-up: How would you solve with a min-heap of size three? What if ties must include all values equal to the third?

Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(k) extra/output space in addition to sorting buffers.

Find missing numbers in a sequence

Solve the problem with a clear input contract and deterministic output.

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;

public class FindMissingNumbersInSequenceJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findMissingNumbersInSequence();
    }

private static void findMissingNumbersInSequence() {
    List<Integer> nums = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 4, 7, 9);
    int start = 1, end = 10;
    Set<Integer> present = new HashSet<Integer>(nums);
    List<Integer> missing = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    if (start <= end) for (long value = start; value <= (long) end; value++) if (!present.contains((int) value)) missing.add((int) value);
    System.out.println(missing);
}
}

Merge lists and remove duplicates

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class MergeListsAndRemoveDuplicatesJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        mergeListsAndRemoveDuplicates();
    }

private static void mergeListsAndRemoveDuplicates() {
    List<List<Integer>> lists = Arrays.asList(Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2), Arrays.asList(3, 4, 1));
    if (lists.contains(null)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("inner lists must not be null");
    List<Integer> merged = lists.stream().flatMap(List::stream).distinct().collect(Collectors.toList());
    System.out.println(merged);
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class MergeListsAndRemoveDuplicatesJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        mergeListsAndRemoveDuplicates();
    }

private static void mergeListsAndRemoveDuplicates() {
    List<List<Integer>> lists = Arrays.asList(Arrays.asList(1, 2, 2), Arrays.asList(3, 4, 1));
    Set<Integer> unique = new LinkedHashSet<Integer>();
    for (List<Integer> list : lists) { if (list == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("inner list must not be null"); unique.addAll(list); }

Explanation and edge cases

Approach: flatMap converts the nested lists into one stream of integers, then distinct retains first occurrences. The Java 7 version collects into LinkedHashSet to preserve encounter order.

Interview follow-up: How would you merge sorted lists efficiently? What is the difference between flatMap and map?

Complexity: O(N) expected time and O(U) space, where N is total input elements and U is unique values.

Q083Array / Collections

Reverse an array in place using two pointers

Reverse the array without allocating a second array.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Easy
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
Expected output
[5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class ReverseArrayInPlaceTwoPointersJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        reverseArrayInPlaceTwoPointers();
    }

private static void reverseArrayInPlaceTwoPointers() {
    int[] values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    for (int left = 0, right = values.length - 1; left < right; left++, right--) {
        int temp = values[left]; values[left] = values[right]; values[right] = temp;
    }
    System.out.println(Arrays.toString(values));
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class ReverseArrayInPlaceTwoPointersJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        reverseArrayInPlaceTwoPointers();
    }

private static void reverseArrayInPlaceTwoPointers() {
    int[] values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    for (int left = 0, right = values.length - 1; left < right; left++, right--) {
        int temp = values[left]; values[left] = values[right]; values[right] = temp;
    }
    System.out.println(Arrays.toString(values));
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Swap the outermost pair and move both pointers inward until they meet. Every pair is swapped exactly once.

Edge cases: Empty and one-element arrays remain unchanged. The input array is modified in place.

Interview follow-up: How would you reverse only a subrange? What is the difference between in-place and auxiliary space?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Q084Array / Collections

Sort an array containing only 0s, 1s and 2s

Sort an array of only 0, 1 and 2 in one pass without using a sorting library.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {2, 0, 2, 1, 1, 0};
Expected output
[0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class SortArrayContainingOnly0s1sAnd2sJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        sortArrayContainingOnly0s1sAnd2s();
    }

private static void sortArrayContainingOnly0s1sAnd2s() {
    int[] a = {2, 0, 2, 1, 1, 0};
    int low = 0, mid = 0, high = a.length - 1;
    while (mid <= high) {
        if (a[mid] == 0) { swap(a, low++, mid++); }
        else if (a[mid] == 1) mid++;
        else if (a[mid] == 2) swap(a, mid, high--);
        else throw new IllegalArgumentException("only 0, 1 and 2 are allowed");
    }
    System.out.println(Arrays.toString(a));
}
static void swap(int[] a, int i, int j) { int t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = t; }
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class SortArrayContainingOnly0s1sAnd2sJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        sortArrayContainingOnly0s1sAnd2s();
    }

private static void sortArrayContainingOnly0s1sAnd2s() {
    int[] a = {2, 0, 2, 1, 1, 0};
    int low = 0, mid = 0, high = a.length - 1;
    while (mid <= high) {
        if (a[mid] == 0) { swap(a, low++, mid++); }
        else if (a[mid] == 1) mid++;
        else if (a[mid] == 2) swap(a, mid, high--);
        else throw new IllegalArgumentException("only 0, 1 and 2 are allowed");
    }
    System.out.println(Arrays.toString(a));
}
static void swap(int[] a, int i, int j) { int t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = t; }
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Maintain three regions: values below low are zero, values between low and mid are one, and values above high are two. The current mid item is classified and placed in its region.

Edge cases: Empty arrays work. Reject values outside 0, 1 and 2. When swapping a 2 from the right, do not increment mid because the swapped-in value is unprocessed.

Interview follow-up: Why is this better than counting and overwriting? Can it be generalized to K categories?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Q085Array / Collections

Find all leaders in an array

An element is a leader if it is greater than or equal to every element to its right. Return leaders in original left-to-right order.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(r) output space for r leaders.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {16, 17, 4, 3, 5, 2};
Expected output
[17, 5, 2]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindAllLeadersInArrayJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findAllLeadersInArray();
    }

private static void findAllLeadersInArray() {
    int[] a = {16, 17, 4, 3, 5, 2};
    List<Integer> reversed = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    int maxFromRight = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
    for (int i = a.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (a[i] >= maxFromRight) { reversed.add(a[i]); maxFromRight = a[i]; }
    Collections.reverse(reversed);
    System.out.println(reversed);
}
}
Java 7 equivalent

import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;

        findAllLeadersInArray();
    }

private static void findAllLeadersInArray() {
    int[] a = {16, 17, 4, 3, 5, 2};
    List<Integer> reversed = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    int maxFromRight = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
    for (int i = a.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (a[i] >= maxFromRight) { reversed.add(a[i]); maxFromRight = a[i]; }
    Collections.reverse(reversed);
    System.out.println(reversed);
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Scan from right to left while tracking the maximum seen so far. Any value greater than or equal to that maximum is a leader. Reverse the collected list for original order.

Edge cases: An empty array returns []. The rightmost element is always a leader. The >= rule means equal values can both be leaders.

Interview follow-up: What if leaders must be strictly greater than all values to the right? Can the extra result reversal be avoided?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(r) output space for r leaders.

Q086Array / Collections

Rearrange positive and negative numbers alternately

Rearrange non-zero positive and negative values to start with positive and alternate signs while preserving relative order within each sign. Append leftovers at the end.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {1, 2, 3, -4, -1, 4};
Expected output
[1, -4, 2, -1, 3, 4]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class RearrangePositiveAndNegativeNumbersAlternatelyJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        rearrangePositiveAndNegativeNumbersAlternately();
    }

private static void rearrangePositiveAndNegativeNumbersAlternately() {
    int[] a = {1, 2, 3, -4, -1, 4};
    List<Integer> positive = new ArrayList<Integer>(), negative = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    for (int value : a) { if (value > 0) positive.add(value); else if (value < 0) negative.add(value); else throw new IllegalArgumentException("zero has no sign in this problem"); }
    int[] result = new int[a.length]; int i = 0, p = 0, n = 0;
    while (p < positive.size() && n < negative.size()) { result[i++] = positive.get(p++); result[i++] = negative.get(n++); }
    while (p < positive.size()) result[i++] = positive.get(p++);
    while (n < negative.size()) result[i++] = negative.get(n++);
    System.out.println(Arrays.toString(result));
}
}

Interview follow-up: How would you rearrange in place? What if alternating should start with negative?

    }

    int[] a = {1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1}; int current = 0, best = 0;

Q088Array / Collections

Find the missing and repeating number

An array contains n values from 1 through n, with exactly one value missing and one value repeated. Find both.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {4, 3, 6, 2, 1, 1};
Expected output
missing=5, repeating=1
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindMissingAndRepeatingNumberJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findMissingAndRepeatingNumber();
    }

private static void findMissingAndRepeatingNumber() {
    int[] a = {4, 3, 6, 2, 1, 1}; int n = a.length;
    int[] count = new int[n + 1];
    for (int value : a) { if (value < 1 || value > n) throw new IllegalArgumentException("value out of range"); count[value]++; }
    int missing = -1, repeating = -1;
    for (int value = 1; value <= n; value++) { if (count[value] == 0) missing = value; if (count[value] == 2) repeating = value; }
    System.out.println("missing=" + missing + ", repeating=" + repeating);
}
}

Interview follow-up: Can you solve in O(1) extra space using XOR? Compare with sum and sum-of-squares formulas.
