Q090Array / Collections

Find the majority element occurring more than n/2 times

Return the element appearing strictly more than half the array length, or null if no such element exists.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2};
Expected output
2
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindMajorityElementOccurringMoreThanN2TimesJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findMajorityElementOccurringMoreThanN2Times();
    }

private static void findMajorityElementOccurringMoreThanN2Times() {
    int[] a = {2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2}; int candidate = 0, votes = 0;
    for (int value : a) { if (votes == 0) candidate = value; votes += value == candidate ? 1 : -1; }
    int count = 0; for (int value : a) if (value == candidate) count++;
    Integer answer = count > a.length / 2 ? candidate : null;
    System.out.println(answer);
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindMajorityElementOccurringMoreThanN2TimesJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findMajorityElementOccurringMoreThanN2Times();
    }

private static void findMajorityElementOccurringMoreThanN2Times() {
    int[] a = {2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2}; int candidate = 0, votes = 0;
    for (int value : a) { if (votes == 0) candidate = value; votes += value == candidate ? 1 : -1; }
    int count = 0; for (int value : a) if (value == candidate) count++;
    Integer answer = count > a.length / 2 ? candidate : null;
    System.out.println(answer);
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Boyer-Moore voting finds a candidate in one pass. A second pass verifies the candidate because a majority is not guaranteed by every arbitrary input.

Edge cases: Empty input returns null. The required condition is strictly greater than n/2, not greater than or equal.

Interview follow-up: Why is the candidate not guaranteed to be a majority? How does the algorithm generalize to elements occurring more than n/3?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Q091Array / Collections

Find all elements appearing more than n/3 times

Return all values appearing strictly more than floor(n/3) times. There can be at most two such values.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {3, 2, 3};
Expected output
[3]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindAllElementsAppearingMoreThanN3TimesJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findAllElementsAppearingMoreThanN3Times();
    }

private static void findAllElementsAppearingMoreThanN3Times() {
    int[] a = {3, 2, 3}; int c1 = 0, c2 = 1, v1 = 0, v2 = 0;
    for (int x : a) { if (x == c1) v1++; else if (x == c2) v2++; else if (v1 == 0) { c1 = x; v1 = 1; } else if (v2 == 0) { c2 = x; v2 = 1; } else { v1--; v2--; } }
    List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>(); int n1 = 0, n2 = 0;
    for (int x : a) { if (x == c1) n1++; else if (x == c2) n2++; }
    if (n1 > a.length / 3) result.add(c1); if (n2 > a.length / 3) result.add(c2);
    System.out.println(result);
}
}

import java.util.stream.*;

import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindAllElementsAppearingMoreThanN3TimesJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findAllElementsAppearingMoreThanN3Times();
    }

private static void findAllElementsAppearingMoreThanN3Times() {
    int[] a = {3, 2, 3}; int c1 = 0, c2 = 1, v1 = 0, v2 = 0;
    for (int x : a) { if (x == c1) v1++; else if (x == c2) v2++; else if (v1 == 0) { c1 = x; v1 = 1; } else if (v2 == 0) { c2 = x; v2 = 1; } else { v1--; v2--; } }
    List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>(); int n1 = 0, n2 = 0;
    for (int x : a) { if (x == c1) n1++; else if (x == c2) n2++; }
    if (n1 > a.length / 3) result.add(c1); if (n2 > a.length / 3) result.add(c2);
    System.out.println(result);
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Use the extended Boyer-Moore algorithm with two candidate slots because at most two values can exceed n/3. Verify both candidates in a second pass.

Edge cases: The result can contain zero, one or two values. Candidate placeholders are not accepted without frequency verification.

Interview follow-up: How would you solve for threshold n/k? Why can at most k-1 values exceed n/k?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

import java.util.*;

public class FindMaximumProductSubarrayJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findMaximumProductSubarray();
    }

private static void findMaximumProductSubarray() {
    int[] a = {2, 3, -2, 4}; int maxEnding = a[0], minEnding = a[0], best = a[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < a.length; i++) {
        int x = a[i]; if (x < 0) { int t = maxEnding; maxEnding = minEnding; minEnding = t; }
        maxEnding = Math.max(x, maxEnding * x); minEnding = Math.min(x, minEnding * x); best = Math.max(best, maxEnding);
    }
    System.out.println(best);
}
}

Q094Array / Collections

Find the next permutation

Rearrange the numbers into the next lexicographically greater permutation. If no greater permutation exists, return the smallest ascending order.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {1, 2, 3};
Expected output
[1, 3, 2]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindNextPermutationJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findNextPermutation();
    }

private static void findNextPermutation() {
    int[] a = {1, 2, 3}; int i = a.length - 2;
    while (i >= 0 && a[i] >= a[i + 1]) i--;
    if (i >= 0) { int j = a.length - 1; while (a[j] <= a[i]) j--; swap(a, i, j); }
    reverse(a, i + 1, a.length - 1);
    System.out.println(Arrays.toString(a));
}
static void swap(int[] a, int i, int j) { int t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = t; }
static void reverse(int[] a, int l, int r) { while (l < r) swap(a, l++, r--); }
}

import java.util.stream.*;

    }

}
static void swap(int[] a, int i, int j) { int t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = t; }
static void reverse(int[] a, int l, int r) { while (l < r) swap(a, l++, r--); }
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Find the rightmost ascending pivot. Swap it with the smallest value greater than it in the suffix (the rightmost such value), then reverse the suffix into ascending order.

Edge cases: Empty or one-element arrays remain unchanged. A descending array wraps to ascending order. Duplicates are supported.

Interview follow-up: Why is the suffix non-increasing before reversal? How does this produce the immediate next permutation?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Q095Array / Collections

Find the smallest missing positive integer

Find the smallest positive integer absent from an unsorted array in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

Complexity: O(n) time because each value can be placed at most once; O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Hard

int[] values = {3, 4, -1, 1};

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindSmallestMissingPositiveIntegerJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findSmallestMissingPositiveInteger();
    }

private static void findSmallestMissingPositiveInteger() {
    int[] a = {3, 4, -1, 1}; int n = a.length;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) while (a[i] >= 1 && a[i] <= n && a[a[i] - 1] != a[i]) {
        int target = a[i] - 1, temp = a[target]; a[target] = a[i]; a[i] = temp;
    }
    int answer = n + 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (a[i] != i + 1) { answer = i + 1; break; }
    System.out.println(answer);
}
}

Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Edge cases: Duplicates are handled by checking whether the target slot already contains the value. Negative, zero and values greater than n are ignored. Empty input returns 1.

Interview follow-up: Why can the answer never exceed n+1? Prove the while loop terminates.

Complexity: O(n) time because each value can be placed at most once; O(1) auxiliary space.

public class FindEquilibriumIndexJava8 {    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findEquilibriumIndex();
    }

private static void findEquilibriumIndex() {
    int[] a = {1, 3, 5, 2, 2}; long total = 0; for (int x : a) total += x;

    for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) { total -= a[i]; if (left == total) { answer = i; break; } left += a[i]; }

Q097Array / Collections

Count subarrays with sum equal to K

Count all contiguous subarrays whose sum equals the target K. Negative numbers are allowed.

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class CountSubarraysSumEqualToKJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        countSubarraysSumEqualToK();
    }

private static void countSubarraysSumEqualToK() {
    int[] a = {1, 1, 1}; int k = 2; Map<Long, Integer> frequency = new HashMap<Long, Integer>();
    frequency.put(0L, 1); long prefix = 0, count = 0;
    for (int x : a) { prefix += x; count += frequency.containsKey(prefix - k) ? frequency.get(prefix - k) : 0; frequency.put(prefix, frequency.containsKey(prefix) ? frequency.get(prefix) + 1 : 1); }
    System.out.println(count);
}
}

Edge cases: Negative numbers are supported, so a sliding window is not generally valid. Long prefix sums avoid many int overflow cases; the count itself may exceed int.

Interview follow-up: Why does sliding window fail when negatives are present? How would you return the actual subarray indexes?

Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(n) space.

Q101Array / Collections

Maximum sum of a subarray of fixed size K

Find the largest sum among all contiguous windows of exactly K elements.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Easy
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 2};
int k = 3;
Expected output
9
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class MaximumSumOfSubarrayOfFixedSizeKJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        maximumSumOfSubarrayOfFixedSizeK();
    }

private static void maximumSumOfSubarrayOfFixedSizeK() {
    int[] a = {2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 2}; int k = 3;
    if (k <= 0 || k > a.length) throw new IllegalArgumentException("invalid window size");
    long sum = 0; for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) sum += a[i]; long best = sum;
    for (int right = k; right < a.length; right++) { sum += a[right] - a[right - k]; best = Math.max(best, sum); }
    System.out.println(best);
}
}

import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;

    long sum = 0; for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) sum += a[i]; long best = sum;

Interview follow-up: How would you return the window boundaries? What changes for a variable-size window with a sum constraint?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Q102Array / Collections

Maximum circular subarray sum

Find the maximum sum of a non-empty subarray in a circular array.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Hard
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {5, -3, 5};
Expected output
10
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class MaximumCircularSubarraySumJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        maximumCircularSubarraySum();
    }

private static void maximumCircularSubarraySum() {
    int[] a = {5, -3, 5}; long total = 0, maxEnd = a[0], maxSum = a[0], minEnd = a[0], minSum = a[0]; total = a[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < a.length; i++) { int x = a[i]; total += x; maxEnd = Math.max(x, maxEnd + x); maxSum = Math.max(maxSum, maxEnd); minEnd = Math.min(x, minEnd + x); minSum = Math.min(minSum, minEnd); }
    long answer = maxSum < 0 ? maxSum : Math.max(maxSum, total - minSum);
    System.out.println(answer);
}
}

    }

private static void maximumCircularSubarraySum() {
    int[] a = {5, -3, 5}; long total = 0, maxEnd = a[0], maxSum = a[0], minEnd = a[0], minSum = a[0]; total = a[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < a.length; i++) { int x = a[i]; total += x; maxEnd = Math.max(x, maxEnd + x); maxSum = Math.max(maxSum, maxEnd); minEnd = Math.min(x, minEnd + x); minSum = Math.min(minSum, minEnd); }
    long answer = maxSum < 0 ? maxSum : Math.max(maxSum, total - minSum);
    System.out.println(answer);
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: The best circular subarray is either the ordinary maximum subarray or the total array minus the minimum-sum subarray. Handle all-negative input separately because choosing the empty complement would be invalid.

Edge cases: Array must be non-empty. All-negative values return the largest element. Long variables reduce sum overflow risk.

Interview follow-up: Why does total minus minimum subarray represent a wrapping subarray? How can Kadane’s algorithm be proved?

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Q103Array / Collections

Container With Most Water

Given vertical line heights, choose two lines that contain the maximum area with the x-axis.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Medium

int[] heights = {1, 8, 6, 2, 5, 4, 8, 3, 7};

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class ContainerMostWaterJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        containerMostWater();
    }

private static void containerMostWater() {
    int[] h = {1, 8, 6, 2, 5, 4, 8, 3, 7}; int left = 0, right = h.length - 1; long best = 0;
    while (left < right) { long area = (long) (right - left) * Math.min(h[left], h[right]); best = Math.max(best, area); if (h[left] < h[right]) left++; else right--; }
    System.out.println(best);
}
}

Q104Array / Collections

Trapping Rain Water

Given bar heights, calculate how much water is trapped after raining.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Hard
Sample input / test data
int[] heights = {4, 2, 0, 3, 2, 5};
Expected output
9
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class TrappingRainWaterJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        trappingRainWater();
    }

private static void trappingRainWater() {
    int[] h = {4, 2, 0, 3, 2, 5}; int left = 0, right = h.length - 1, leftMax = 0, rightMax = 0; long water = 0;
    while (left < right) {
        if (h[left] <= h[right]) { if (h[left] >= leftMax) leftMax = h[left]; else water += leftMax - h[left]; left++; }
        else { if (h[right] >= rightMax) rightMax = h[right]; else water += rightMax - h[right]; right--; }
    }
    System.out.println(water);
}
}

Edge cases: Empty and one-element arrays trap zero water. Heights must be non-negative. Use long for total volume.

Interview follow-up: How does the prefix-max/suffix-max O(n) space solution work? Why can the smaller side be finalized?

Q105Array / Collections

Find floor and ceiling in a sorted array

For a sorted ascending array, find the greatest value <= x and the smallest value >= x.

Complexity: O(log n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Easy
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {1, 2, 8, 10, 10, 12, 19};
int x = 5;
Expected output
floor=2, ceiling=8
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindFloorAndCeilingInSortedArrayJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findFloorAndCeilingInSortedArray();
    }

private static void findFloorAndCeilingInSortedArray() {
    int[] a = {1, 2, 8, 10, 10, 12, 19}; int x = 5; int floor = -1, ceiling = -1;
    int lo = 0, hi = a.length - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) { int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if (a[mid] <= x) { floor = a[mid]; lo = mid + 1; } else hi = mid - 1; }
    lo = 0; hi = a.length - 1;
    while (lo <= hi) { int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if (a[mid] >= x) { ceiling = a[mid]; hi = mid - 1; } else lo = mid + 1; }
    System.out.println("floor=" + floor + ", ceiling=" + ceiling);
}
}

}

Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Run two binary searches: an upper-bound style search for the last value <= x, and a lower-bound style search for the first value >= x.

Edge cases: Return -1 when a floor or ceiling does not exist. Duplicates are supported. Input must be sorted ascending.

Interview follow-up: How do lowerBound and upperBound differ? How can both searches be combined into one pass?

Complexity: O(log n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

    }

    int[] a = {1, 2, 3, 1}; int lo = 0, hi = a.length - 1;
    while (lo < hi) { int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if (a[mid] < a[mid + 1]) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid; }

Q107Array / Collections

Merge two sorted arrays without extra space

Given two sorted arrays, rearrange their values so the first contains the smallest m values and the second contains the remaining n values.

Complexity: O((m+n) log(m+n)) comparisons in this implementation; O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
int[] first = {1, 4, 7, 8, 10};
int[] second = {2, 3, 9};
Expected output
first=[1, 2, 3, 4, 7]
second=[8, 9, 10]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class MergeTwoSortedArraysWithoutExtraSpaceJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        mergeTwoSortedArraysWithoutExtraSpace();
    }

private static void mergeTwoSortedArraysWithoutExtraSpace() {
    int[] a = {1, 4, 7, 8, 10}, b = {2, 3, 9}; int total = a.length + b.length;
    for (int gap = nextGap(total); gap > 0; gap = nextGap(gap)) {
        for (int i = 0, j = gap; j < total; i++, j++) {
            int x = get(a, b, i), y = get(a, b, j);
            if (x > y) { set(a, b, i, y); set(a, b, j, x); }
        }
    }
    System.out.println("first=" + Arrays.toString(a)); System.out.println("second=" + Arrays.toString(b));
}
static int nextGap(int gap) { return gap <= 1 ? 0 : (gap / 2) + (gap % 2); }
static int get(int[] a, int[] b, int i) { return i < a.length ? a[i] : b[i - a.length]; }
static void set(int[] a, int[] b, int i, int v) { if (i < a.length) a[i] = v; else b[i - a.length] = v; }
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class MergeTwoSortedArraysWithoutExtraSpaceJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        mergeTwoSortedArraysWithoutExtraSpace();
    }

private static void mergeTwoSortedArraysWithoutExtraSpace() {
    int[] a = {1, 4, 7, 8, 10}, b = {2, 3, 9}; int total = a.length + b.length;
    for (int gap = nextGap(total); gap > 0; gap = nextGap(gap)) {
        for (int i = 0, j = gap; j < total; i++, j++) {
            int x = get(a, b, i), y = get(a, b, j);
            if (x > y) { set(a, b, i, y); set(a, b, j, x); }
        }
    }
    System.out.println("first=" + Arrays.toString(a)); System.out.println("second=" + Arrays.toString(b));
}
static int nextGap(int gap) { return gap <= 1 ? 0 : (gap / 2) + (gap % 2); }
static int get(int[] a, int[] b, int i) { return i < a.length ? a[i] : b[i - a.length]; }
static void set(int[] a, int[] b, int i, int v) { if (i < a.length) a[i] = v; else b[i - a.length] = v; }
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Treat both arrays as one virtual sequence. Apply Shell-sort-style gap comparisons across both arrays, reducing the gap until one. No third array is allocated.

Edge cases: Both arrays must already be sorted. Empty arrays work. The method mutates both arrays. This is a comparison-based gap method; a simpler O((m+n) log(m+n)) alternative concatenates and sorts.

Interview follow-up: Can you derive the gap sequence? What is the complexity of the gap method versus a heap merge?

Complexity: O((m+n) log(m+n)) comparisons in this implementation; O(1) auxiliary space.

Q108Array / Collections

Count inversions using merge sort

Count pairs (i,j) where i < j and a[i] > a[j].

Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Hard
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {2, 4, 1, 3, 5};
Expected output
3
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class CountInversionsMergeSortJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        countInversionsMergeSort();
    }

private static void countInversionsMergeSort() {
    int[] a = {2, 4, 1, 3, 5}; int[] temp = new int[a.length];
    System.out.println(count(a, temp, 0, a.length - 1));
}
static long count(int[] a, int[] t, int lo, int hi) {
    if (lo >= hi) return 0; int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
    long total = count(a, t, lo, mid) + count(a, t, mid + 1, hi); int i = lo, j = mid + 1, k = lo;
    while (i <= mid && j <= hi) { if (a[i] <= a[j]) t[k++] = a[i++]; else { t[k++] = a[j++]; total += mid - i + 1; } }
    while (i <= mid) t[k++] = a[i++]; while (j <= hi) t[k++] = a[j++];
    for (i = lo; i <= hi; i++) a[i] = t[i]; return total;
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class CountInversionsMergeSortJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        countInversionsMergeSort();
    }

private static void countInversionsMergeSort() {
    int[] a = {2, 4, 1, 3, 5}; int[] temp = new int[a.length];
    System.out.println(count(a, temp, 0, a.length - 1));
}
static long count(int[] a, int[] t, int lo, int hi) {
    if (lo >= hi) return 0; int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
    long total = count(a, t, lo, mid) + count(a, t, mid + 1, hi); int i = lo, j = mid + 1, k = lo;
    while (i <= mid && j <= hi) { if (a[i] <= a[j]) t[k++] = a[i++]; else { t[k++] = a[j++]; total += mid - i + 1; } }
    while (i <= mid) t[k++] = a[i++]; while (j <= hi) t[k++] = a[j++];
    for (i = lo; i <= hi; i++) a[i] = t[i]; return total;
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Divide the array, count inversions in each half, then merge. When a right-half value is smaller than the current left value, it is smaller than every remaining left value, so add mid-i+1 inversions.

Edge cases: Equal values are not inversions; use <= in the merge comparison. Empty and one-element arrays return zero. Use long for the count.

Interview follow-up: Why is merge sort suitable for counting inversions? Can a Fenwick tree solve the problem?

Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.

import java.util.*;

import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class SortKSortedArrayPriorityQueueJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        sortKSortedArrayPriorityQueue();
    }

private static void sortKSortedArrayPriorityQueue() {
    int[] a = {6, 5, 3, 2, 8, 10, 9}; int k = 3;
    PriorityQueue<Integer> heap = new PriorityQueue<Integer>(); int out = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) { heap.offer(a[i]); if (heap.size() > k) a[out++] = heap.poll(); }
    while (!heap.isEmpty()) a[out++] = heap.poll();
    System.out.println(Arrays.toString(a));
}
}

Q110Array / Collections

Allocate minimum pages among students

Allocate contiguous book pages to exactly M students, minimizing the maximum pages assigned to any student. Each student must receive at least one book.

Complexity: O(n log(sum of pages)) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Hard
Sample input / test data
int[] pages = {12, 34, 67, 90};
int students = 2;
Expected output
113
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class AllocateMinimumPagesAmongStudentsJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        allocateMinimumPagesAmongStudents();
    }

private static void allocateMinimumPagesAmongStudents() {
    int[] pages = {12, 34, 67, 90}; int students = 2;
    if (students <= 0 || students > pages.length) throw new IllegalArgumentException("invalid student count");
    long low = 0, high = 0; for (int p : pages) { if (p < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("negative pages"); low = Math.max(low, p); high += p; }
    while (low < high) { long mid = low + (high - low) / 2; if (canAllocate(pages, students, mid)) high = mid; else low = mid + 1; }
    System.out.println(low);
}
static boolean canAllocate(int[] pages, int students, long limit) {
    int used = 1; long sum = 0;
    for (int p : pages) { if (sum + p > limit) { used++; sum = p; if (used > students) return false; } else sum += p; }
    return true;
}
}

import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;

    }

}
static boolean canAllocate(int[] pages, int students, long limit) {

Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Binary search the answer between the largest single book and the total pages. A greedy feasibility check counts how many students are needed if no student may exceed the candidate limit.

Edge cases: Requires 1 <= students <= number of books and non-negative page counts. If students exceed books, the classic contiguous allocation problem is invalid.

Interview follow-up: Why is the feasibility function monotonic? How does this pattern apply to shipping capacity and split-array largest sum?

Complexity: O(n log(sum of pages)) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Q112Array / Collections

Rotate a square matrix 90 degrees clockwise

Rotate an N by N matrix in place by 90 degrees clockwise.

Complexity: O(n²) time and O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
int[][] matrix = {{1,2,3},{4,5,6},{7,8,9}};
Expected output
[[7, 4, 1], [8, 5, 2], [9, 6, 3]]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class RotateSquareMatrix90DegreesClockwiseJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        rotateSquareMatrix90DegreesClockwise();
    }

private static void rotateSquareMatrix90DegreesClockwise() {
    int[][] a = {{1,2,3},{4,5,6},{7,8,9}}; int n = a.length;
    for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) for (int c = r + 1; c < n; c++) { int t = a[r][c]; a[r][c] = a[c][r]; a[c][r] = t; }
    for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) for (int l = 0, h = n - 1; l < h; l++, h--) { int t = a[r][l]; a[r][l] = a[r][h]; a[r][h] = t; }
    System.out.println(Arrays.deepToString(a));
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

import java.math.*;

    }

private static void rotateSquareMatrix90DegreesClockwise() {
    int[][] a = {{1,2,3},{4,5,6},{7,8,9}}; int n = a.length;
    for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) for (int c = r + 1; c < n; c++) { int t = a[r][c]; a[r][c] = a[c][r]; a[c][r] = t; }
    for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) for (int l = 0, h = n - 1; l < h; l++, h--) { int t = a[r][l]; a[r][l] = a[r][h]; a[r][h] = t; }
    System.out.println(Arrays.deepToString(a));
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Transpose the matrix across its main diagonal, then reverse every row. Both transformations are in place.

Edge cases: Matrix must be square. Empty and 1x1 matrices remain unchanged.

Interview follow-up: How would you rotate counterclockwise? Can you rotate layer by layer without transpose?

Complexity: O(n²) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Validate a partially filled Sudoku board

Determine whether a 9x9 Sudoku board is valid: no duplicate digit may occur in any row, column or 3x3 box. Empty cells are represented by dot.

Complexity: O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space for fixed 9x9 size; O(R×C) if generalized.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data

 {'5','3','.','.','7','.','.','.','.'},

 {'7','.','.','.','2','.','.','.','6'},
 {'.','6','.','.','.','.','2','8','.'},
 {'.','.','.','4','1','9','.','.','5'},
 {'.','.','.','.','8','.','.','7','9'}
};
Expected output
true
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class ValidatePartiallyFilledSudokuBoardJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        validatePartiallyFilledSudokuBoard();
    }

private static void validatePartiallyFilledSudokuBoard() {
    char[][] b = {{'5','3','.','.','7','.','.','.','.'},{'6','.','.','1','9','5','.','.','.'},{'.','9','8','.','.','.','.','6','.'},{'8','.','.','.','6','.','.','.','3'},{'4','.','.','8','.','3','.','.','1'},{'7','.','.','.','2','.','.','.','6'},{'.','6','.','.','.','.','2','8','.'},{'.','.','.','4','1','9','.','.','5'},{'.','.','.','.','8','.','.','7','9'}};
    boolean valid = true; boolean[][] rows = new boolean[9][9], cols = new boolean[9][9], boxes = new boolean[9][9];
    for (int r = 0; r < 9 && valid; r++) for (int c = 0; c < 9; c++) { char ch = b[r][c]; if (ch == '.') continue;
        if (ch < '1' || ch > '9') { valid = false; break; } int d = ch - '1', box = (r / 3) * 3 + c / 3;
        if (rows[r][d] || cols[c][d] || boxes[box][d]) { valid = false; break; }
        rows[r][d] = cols[c][d] = boxes[box][d] = true;
    }
    System.out.println(valid);
}
}

Q117Array / Collections

Find the median in a row-wise sorted matrix

Find the median of a matrix where each row is sorted ascending and total element count is odd.

Complexity: O(R log C log V) time, where V is the value range; O(1) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Hard
Sample input / test data
int[][] matrix = {{1,3,5},{2,6,9},{3,6,9}};
Expected output
5
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindMedianInRowWiseSortedMatrixJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findMedianInRowWiseSortedMatrix();
    }

private static void findMedianInRowWiseSortedMatrix() {
    int[][] a = {{1,3,5},{2,6,9},{3,6,9}}; int rows = a.length, cols = a[0].length;
    int low = Integer.MAX_VALUE, high = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) { low = Math.min(low, a[r][0]); high = Math.max(high, a[r][cols - 1]); }
    int desired = (rows * cols + 1) / 2;
    while (low < high) { int mid = low + (int)(((long)high - low) / 2); int count = 0;
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) count += upperBound(a[r], mid);
        if (count < desired) low = mid + 1; else high = mid;
    }
    System.out.println(low);
}
static int upperBound(int[] row, int x) { int lo = 0, hi = row.length; while (lo < hi) { int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if (row[mid] <= x) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid; } return lo; }
}

static int upperBound(int[] row, int x) { int lo = 0, hi = row.length; while (lo < hi) { int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if (row[mid] <= x) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid; } return lo; }
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Binary search the value range between the smallest first element and largest last element. For each midpoint, count values <= midpoint using upperBound in every sorted row.

Edge cases: Assumes non-empty rectangular rows, each row sorted, and odd total element count. Even-sized matrices need a stated median convention.

Interview follow-up: Why binary search values rather than indexes? How would you handle an even number of elements?

Complexity: O(R log C log V) time, where V is the value range; O(1) auxiliary space.

Find Kth smallest in a row-and-column sorted matrix

Complexity: O(k log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.Difficulty: Hard
Sample input / test data
int[][] matrix = {{1,5,9},{10,11,13},{12,13,15}};
int k = 8;
Expected output
13
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindKthSmallestInRowAndColumnSortedMatrixJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findKthSmallestInRowAndColumnSortedMatrix();
    }

private static void findKthSmallestInRowAndColumnSortedMatrix() {
    int[][] a = {{1,5,9},{10,11,13},{12,13,15}}; int k = 8, n = a.length;
    PriorityQueue<int[]> heap = new PriorityQueue<int[]>(new Comparator<int[]>() { public int compare(int[] x, int[] y) { return Integer.compare(x[0], y[0]); } });
    for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) heap.offer(new int[]{a[r][0], r, 0}); int value = -1;
    for (int count = 0; count < k; count++) { int[] item = heap.poll(); value = item[0]; int r = item[1], c = item[2]; if (c + 1 < n) heap.offer(new int[]{a[r][c + 1], r, c + 1}); }
    System.out.println(value);
}
}

Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Seed a min-heap with the first element of each row. Repeatedly extract the smallest and insert the next element from that same row. The Kth extracted value is the answer.

Edge cases: Assumes a non-empty square matrix and 1 <= K <= n². For rectangular matrices, seed each row and check column bounds against that row length.

Interview follow-up: How does value-domain binary search solve this problem? Compare O(k log n) heap work with binary-search counting.

Complexity: O(k log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.

import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class FindUniquePairsGivenDifferenceKJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findUniquePairsGivenDifferenceK();
    }

private static void findUniquePairsGivenDifferenceK() {
    int[] a = {1, 5, 3, 4, 2}; int k = 3; if (k <= 0) { System.out.println(0); return; } Set<Integer> values = new HashSet<Integer>(); for (int x : a) values.add(x);
    Set<String> pairs = new HashSet<String>();
    for (int x : values) { long y = (long)x + Math.abs((long)k); if (y <= Integer.MAX_VALUE && y >= Integer.MIN_VALUE && values.contains((int)y)) pairs.add(x + ":" + (int)y); }
    System.out.println(pairs.size());
}
}

Sample input / test data

import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindAllUniqueTripletsWhoseSumEqualsTargetJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findAllUniqueTripletsWhoseSumEqualsTarget();
    }

private static void findAllUniqueTripletsWhoseSumEqualsTarget() {
    int[] a = {-1, 0, 1, 2, -1, -4}; int target = 0; Arrays.sort(a); List<List<Integer>> result = new ArrayList<List<Integer>>();
    for (int i = 0; i < a.length - 2; i++) { if (i > 0 && a[i] == a[i - 1]) continue; int l = i + 1, r = a.length - 1;
        while (l < r) { long sum = (long)a[i] + a[l] + a[r]; if (sum == target) { result.add(Arrays.asList(a[i], a[l], a[r])); int left = a[l], right = a[r]; while (l < r && a[l] == left) l++; while (l < r && a[r] == right) r--; } else if (sum < target) l++; else r--; }
    }
    System.out.println(result);
}
}

    int[] a = {-1, 0, 1, 2, -1, -4}; int target = 0; Arrays.sort(a); List<List<Integer>> result = new ArrayList<List<Integer>>();
    for (int i = 0; i < a.length - 2; i++) { if (i > 0 && a[i] == a[i - 1]) continue; int l = i + 1, r = a.length - 1;
        while (l < r) { long sum = (long)a[i] + a[l] + a[r]; if (sum == target) { result.add(Arrays.asList(a[i], a[l], a[r])); int left = a[l], right = a[r]; while (l < r && a[l] == left) l++; while (l < r && a[r] == right) r--; } else if (sum < target) l++; else r--; }
    }
    System.out.println(result);
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Sort the array. Fix one element, then use two pointers to find the remaining pair. Skip duplicate fixed values and duplicate left/right values to avoid repeated triplets.

Edge cases: Fewer than three elements returns []. Use long for the sum to avoid integer overflow. Output triplets are sorted and unique.

Interview follow-up: How would you generalize to 4Sum? What is the brute-force complexity?

Complexity: O(n²) time and O(1) auxiliary space excluding sort and output (sorting may use implementation-specific space).

Q121Array / Collections

Count possible triangles from array elements

Count triplets that can be side lengths of a non-degenerate triangle: the sum of the two smaller sides must be greater than the largest.

Complexity: O(n²) time and O(1) auxiliary space excluding sort.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
int[] sides = {4, 6, 3, 7};
Expected output
3
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class CountPossibleTrianglesArrayElementsJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        countPossibleTrianglesArrayElements();
    }

private static void countPossibleTrianglesArrayElements() {
    int[] a = {4, 6, 3, 7}; Arrays.sort(a); long count = 0;
    for (int k = a.length - 1; k >= 2; k--) { int l = 0, r = k - 1; while (l < r) { if ((long)a[l] + a[r] > a[k]) { count += r - l; r--; } else l++; } }
    System.out.println(count);
}
}

Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Sort ascending and fix the largest side k. If a[l]+a[r] exceeds a[k], then every index from l to r-1 paired with r also forms a triangle, so add r-l and move r left.

Edge cases: All side lengths must be positive. Duplicate side lengths represent separate indexed elements. Strict greater-than is required for a non-degenerate triangle.

Interview follow-up: Why can r-l combinations be counted at once? How would you return the actual triples?

Complexity: O(n²) time and O(1) auxiliary space excluding sort.

    }

private static void checkDuplicatesWithinDistanceK() {
    int[] a = {1, 2, 3, 1}; int k = 3; Set<Integer> window = new HashSet<Integer>(); boolean found = false;
    if (k <= 0) { System.out.println(false); return; }
    for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) { if (window.contains(a[i])) { found = true; break; } window.add(a[i]); if (window.size() > k) window.remove(a[i - k]); }

}
}

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class CountDistinctElementsInEveryWindowOfSizeKJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        countDistinctElementsInEveryWindowOfSizeK();
    }

private static void countDistinctElementsInEveryWindowOfSizeK() {
    int[] a = {1, 2, 1, 3, 4, 2, 3}; int k = 3;
    if (k <= 0 || k > a.length) throw new IllegalArgumentException("invalid window size");
    Map<Integer, Integer> frequency = new HashMap<Integer, Integer>(); List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) { frequency.put(a[i], frequency.containsKey(a[i]) ? frequency.get(a[i]) + 1 : 1);
        if (i >= k) { int out = a[i - k], next = frequency.get(out) - 1; if (next == 0) frequency.remove(out); else frequency.put(out, next); }
        if (i >= k - 1) result.add(frequency.size());
    }
    System.out.println(result);
}
}

Q124Array / Collections

Implement a Stack using two Queues

Implement stack push and pop using two queues. Use the costly-push approach.

Complexity: push O(n), pop O(1), O(n) space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
push(1), push(2), push(3), pop(), pop(), pop()
Expected output
3, 2, 1
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class ImplementStackTwoQueuesJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        implementStackTwoQueues();
    }

static class StackViaQueues {
    Queue<Integer> q1 = new ArrayDeque<Integer>(), q2 = new ArrayDeque<Integer>();
    void push(int value) { q2.offer(value); while (!q1.isEmpty()) q2.offer(q1.poll()); Queue<Integer> t = q1; q1 = q2; q2 = t; }
    Integer pop() { return q1.poll(); }
}
private static void implementStackTwoQueues() {
    StackViaQueues stack = new StackViaQueues(); stack.push(1); stack.push(2); stack.push(3);
    System.out.println(stack.pop() + ", " + stack.pop() + ", " + stack.pop());
}
}

Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: On push, enqueue the new value into the empty auxiliary queue, then move all old values behind it. Swap the queue references so the newest value stays at the front.

Edge cases: pop on an empty stack returns null in this example; a production API may throw NoSuchElementException. ArrayDeque does not allow null elements.

Interview follow-up: What is the alternative costly-pop approach? Compare operation complexities.

Complexity: push O(n), pop O(1), O(n) space.

Q125Array / Collections

Complexity: Amortized O(1) enqueue/dequeue; O(n) worst-case for a single transfer; O(n) space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class ImplementQueueTwoStacksJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        implementQueueTwoStacks();
    }

static class QueueViaStacks {
    Deque<Integer> incoming = new ArrayDeque<Integer>(), outgoing = new ArrayDeque<Integer>();
    void enqueue(int value) { incoming.push(value); }
    Integer dequeue() { if (outgoing.isEmpty()) while (!incoming.isEmpty()) outgoing.push(incoming.pop()); return outgoing.poll(); }
}
private static void implementQueueTwoStacks() {
    QueueViaStacks queue = new QueueViaStacks(); queue.enqueue(1); queue.enqueue(2); queue.enqueue(3);
    System.out.println(queue.dequeue() + ", " + queue.dequeue() + ", " + queue.dequeue());
}
}

Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Push new items onto the incoming stack. When dequeue needs an item and outgoing is empty, move all incoming items to outgoing; this reverses order and exposes the oldest item.

Edge cases: Empty dequeue returns null in this example. Each item moves between stacks at most once, which gives amortized O(1) dequeue.

Interview follow-up: Why is the amortized complexity O(1) even though one dequeue can take O(n)? How would you implement peek?

Complexity: Amortized O(1) enqueue/dequeue; O(n) worst-case for a single transfer; O(n) space.

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class DesignMinStackOGetMinJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        designMinStackOGetMin();
    }

static class MinStack {
    Deque<Integer> values = new ArrayDeque<Integer>(), mins = new ArrayDeque<Integer>();
    void push(int x) { values.push(x); if (mins.isEmpty() || x <= mins.peek()) mins.push(x); }
    Integer pop() { if (values.isEmpty()) return null; int x = values.pop(); if (x == mins.peek()) mins.pop(); return x; }
    Integer top() { return values.peek(); }
    Integer getMin() { return mins.peek(); }
}
private static void designMinStackOGetMin() {
    MinStack s = new MinStack(); s.push(3); s.push(5); s.push(2); s.push(1);
    System.out.println(s.getMin()); s.pop(); System.out.println(s.getMin());
}
}

Approach: Maintain a second stack of minimum values. Push a value onto mins whenever it is <= the current minimum; when that value is popped from the main stack, pop it from mins too. The <= handles duplicate minima.

Edge cases: Empty operations return null here. A production implementation may throw. Null is not accepted by ArrayDeque.

Interview follow-up: Can you implement a MinStack using one stack and encoded values? What overflow risk does that approach have?

Complexity: O(1) worst-case time per operation and O(n) space.

Q127Array / Collections

Implement a Circular Queue using an array

Complexity: O(1) time per operation and O(capacity) storage.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
capacity=3; enqueue(1), enqueue(2), enqueue(3), dequeue(), enqueue(4)
Expected output

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class ImplementCircularQueueArrayJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        implementCircularQueueArray();
    }

static class CircularQueue {
    int[] data; int head = 0, size = 0;
    CircularQueue(int capacity) { if (capacity <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException(); data = new int[capacity]; }
    boolean enqueue(int x) { if (size == data.length) return false; data[(head + size) % data.length] = x; size++; return true; }
    Integer dequeue() { if (size == 0) return null; int value = data[head]; head = (head + 1) % data.length; size--; return value; }
    Integer front() { return size == 0 ? null : data[head]; }
    Integer rear() { return size == 0 ? null : data[(head + size - 1) % data.length]; }
}
private static void implementCircularQueueArray() {
    CircularQueue q = new CircularQueue(3); q.enqueue(1); q.enqueue(2); q.enqueue(3); q.dequeue(); q.enqueue(4);
    System.out.println("front=" + q.front() + ", rear=" + q.rear());
}
}

Approach: Track the head index and number of stored items. Insert at (head+size) modulo capacity; advance head modulo capacity on dequeue.

Edge cases: Capacity must be positive. This implementation distinguishes full and empty using size, so all array slots can be used. enqueue returns false when full; dequeue returns null when empty.

Interview follow-up: How would you implement with head/tail pointers and a reserved empty slot? How can this be made thread-safe?

Complexity: O(1) time per operation and O(capacity) storage.

Q128Array / Collections

Merge K sorted arrays using PriorityQueue

Merge multiple sorted arrays into one globally sorted result.

Complexity: O(N log K) time and O(K + N output) space, for N total values and K arrays.Difficulty: Hard
Sample input / test data
int[][] arrays = {{1,4,7},{2,5,8},{3,6,9}};
Expected output
[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class MergeKSortedArraysPriorityQueueJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        mergeKSortedArraysPriorityQueue();
    }

static class Cursor { int value, row, col; Cursor(int v, int r, int c) { value=v; row=r; col=c; } }
private static void mergeKSortedArraysPriorityQueue() {
    int[][] arrays = {{1,4,7},{2,5,8},{3,6,9}};
    PriorityQueue<Cursor> heap = new PriorityQueue<Cursor>(new Comparator<Cursor>() { public int compare(Cursor a, Cursor b) { return Integer.compare(a.value, b.value); } });
    int total = 0; for (int r = 0; r < arrays.length; r++) { total += arrays[r].length; if (arrays[r].length > 0) heap.offer(new Cursor(arrays[r][0], r, 0)); }
    List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
    while (!heap.isEmpty()) { Cursor c = heap.poll(); result.add(c.value); int next = c.col + 1; if (next < arrays[c.row].length) heap.offer(new Cursor(arrays[c.row][next], c.row, next)); }
    System.out.println(result);
}
}

    System.out.println(result);
}

Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Seed a min-heap with the first value from each non-empty array. Remove the smallest cursor, append its value, then insert the next value from that cursor’s array.

Edge cases: Empty arrays are ignored. All input arrays must be sorted ascending. Duplicate values are retained.

Interview follow-up: How does this compare with concatenating and sorting all values? What is the heap size bound?

Complexity: O(N log K) time and O(K + N output) space, for N total values and K arrays.

Q129Array / Collections

Find the running median using two Heaps

After each incoming number, output the median of all values seen so far.

Complexity: O(log n) per insertion and O(1) median lookup; O(n) total storage.Difficulty: Hard
Sample input / test data
int[] stream = {5, 15, 1, 3};
Expected output
[5.0, 10.0, 5.0, 4.0]
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class FindRunningMedianTwoHeapsJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        findRunningMedianTwoHeaps();
    }

private static void findRunningMedianTwoHeaps() {
    int[] stream = {5, 15, 1, 3};
    PriorityQueue<Integer> lower = new PriorityQueue<Integer>(Collections.reverseOrder());
    PriorityQueue<Integer> upper = new PriorityQueue<Integer>(); List<Double> medians = new ArrayList<Double>();
    for (int x : stream) {
        if (lower.isEmpty() || x <= lower.peek()) lower.offer(x); else upper.offer(x);
        if (lower.size() > upper.size() + 1) upper.offer(lower.poll());
        else if (upper.size() > lower.size()) lower.offer(upper.poll());
        double median = lower.size() == upper.size() ? ((long)lower.peek() + upper.peek()) / 2.0 : lower.peek();
        medians.add(median);
    }
    System.out.println(medians);
}
}

import java.util.stream.*;

    PriorityQueue<Integer> upper = new PriorityQueue<Integer>(); List<Double> medians = new ArrayList<Double>();
    for (int x : stream) {

Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Keep the lower half in a max-heap and the upper half in a min-heap. Maintain size difference at most one and ensure every lower value is <= every upper value. The median is the top value(s).

Edge cases: Empty stream has no median. Long addition avoids overflow when averaging two extreme ints. Duplicate values are supported.

Interview follow-up: Why do we use two heaps? How would you support deletion of arbitrary values from the sliding median?

Complexity: O(log n) per insertion and O(1) median lookup; O(n) total storage.

Q130Array / Collections

Sort a Map by values with deterministic tie-breaking

Sort entries by value descending, then by key ascending, and retain that order in the resulting map.

Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) extra space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
Map<String, Integer> scores = new HashMap<String, Integer>();
scores.put("b", 2); scores.put("a", 3); scores.put("c", 2);
Expected output
{a=3, b=2, c=2}
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class SortMapByValuesDeterministicTieBreakingJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        sortMapByValuesDeterministicTieBreaking();
    }

private static void sortMapByValuesDeterministicTieBreaking() {
    Map<String, Integer> scores = new HashMap<String, Integer>(); scores.put("b", 2); scores.put("a", 3); scores.put("c", 2);
    Map<String, Integer> sorted = scores.entrySet().stream()
        .sorted(Map.Entry.<String, Integer>comparingByValue().reversed().thenComparing(Map.Entry.comparingByKey()))
        .collect(Collectors.toMap(Map.Entry::getKey, Map.Entry::getValue, (x, y) -> x, LinkedHashMap::new));
    System.out.println(sorted);
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class SortMapByValuesDeterministicTieBreakingJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        sortMapByValuesDeterministicTieBreaking();
    }

private static void sortMapByValuesDeterministicTieBreaking() {
    Map<String, Integer> scores = new HashMap<String, Integer>(); scores.put("b", 2); scores.put("a", 3); scores.put("c", 2);
    List<Map.Entry<String, Integer>> entries = new ArrayList<Map.Entry<String, Integer>>(scores.entrySet());
    Collections.sort(entries, new Comparator<Map.Entry<String, Integer>>() { public int compare(Map.Entry<String, Integer> x, Map.Entry<String, Integer> y) { int c = Integer.compare(y.getValue(), x.getValue()); return c != 0 ? c : x.getKey().compareTo(y.getKey()); } });
    Map<String, Integer> sorted = new LinkedHashMap<String, Integer>(); for (Map.Entry<String, Integer> e : entries) sorted.put(e.getKey(), e.getValue());
    System.out.println(sorted);
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Sort map entries by descending value and then ascending key. Collect into LinkedHashMap because HashMap does not preserve the sorted encounter order.

Edge cases: Keys must be non-null strings and values non-null integers in this example. The original map is not mutated.

Interview follow-up: Why can’t a HashMap be used for the result? How would you sort by multiple value fields?

Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) extra space.

Q131Array / Collections

Merge two Maps with Map.merge and a duplicate-key policy

Merge two maps by summing values for duplicate keys.

Complexity: O(n + m) expected time and O(n + m) space.Difficulty: Medium
Sample input / test data
Map<String, Integer> first = new LinkedHashMap<String, Integer>(); first.put("a", 1); first.put("b", 2);
Map<String, Integer> second = new LinkedHashMap<String, Integer>(); second.put("a", 3); second.put("b", 4); second.put("c", 5);
Expected output
{a=4, b=6, c=5}
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class MergeTwoMapsMapMergeAndDuplicateKeyPolicyJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        mergeTwoMapsMapMergeAndDuplicateKeyPolicy();
    }

private static void mergeTwoMapsMapMergeAndDuplicateKeyPolicy() {
    Map<String, Integer> first = new LinkedHashMap<String, Integer>(); first.put("a", 1); first.put("b", 2);
    Map<String, Integer> second = new LinkedHashMap<String, Integer>(); second.put("a", 3); second.put("b", 4); second.put("c", 5);
    Map<String, Integer> merged = new LinkedHashMap<String, Integer>(first);
    second.forEach((key, value) -> merged.merge(key, value, Integer::sum));
    System.out.println(merged);
}
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.math.*;
import java.util.regex.*;

public class MergeTwoMapsMapMergeAndDuplicateKeyPolicyJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        mergeTwoMapsMapMergeAndDuplicateKeyPolicy();
    }

private static void mergeTwoMapsMapMergeAndDuplicateKeyPolicy() {
    Map<String, Integer> first = new LinkedHashMap<String, Integer>(); first.put("a", 1); first.put("b", 2);
    Map<String, Integer> second = new LinkedHashMap<String, Integer>(); second.put("a", 3); second.put("b", 4); second.put("c", 5);
    Map<String, Integer> merged = new LinkedHashMap<String, Integer>(first);
    for (Map.Entry<String, Integer> e : second.entrySet()) { String key = e.getKey(); Integer value = e.getValue(); merged.put(key, merged.containsKey(key) ? merged.get(key) + value : value); }
    System.out.println(merged);
}
}
Code explanation, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Copy the first map, then merge each entry from the second. Map.merge inserts a new value when the key is absent and applies the remapping function when it already exists.

Edge cases: The example uses non-null keys and values. LinkedHashMap preserves first insertion order; existing keys retain their position when updated.

Interview follow-up: How would you merge by maximum instead of sum? What does Map.merge do if the remapping function returns null?

Complexity: O(n + m) expected time and O(n + m) space.

Q132Numbers

Check whether a number is prime

Implement the mathematical operation and validate the input domain.

Complexity: O(sqrt(n)) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
int n = 29;
Expected output
29 -> true
Java 8 solution
import java.util.stream.IntStream;

public class CheckWhetherNumberIsPrimeJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 29;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + isPrime(number));
    }

    private static boolean isPrime(int number) {
        return number >= 2 &&
            IntStream.rangeClosed(2, (int) Math.sqrt(number))
                .noneMatch(divisor -> number % divisor == 0);
    }
}
Java 7 equivalent
public class CheckWhetherNumberIsPrimeJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 29;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + isPrime(number));
    }

    private static boolean isPrime(int number) {
        if (number < 2) return false;
        for (int divisor = 2; divisor <= Math.sqrt(number); divisor++) {
            if (number % divisor == 0) return false;
        }
        return true;
    }
}

Generate Fibonacci series

Sample input / test data
int count = 6;  // number of Fibonacci terms to generate
Expected output
0,1,1,2,3,5
Java 8 solution
import java.util.*; import java.util.stream.*;

public class GenerateFibonacciSeriesJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int termCount = 6;
        System.out.println(generateFibonacciSeries(termCount).toString().replaceAll("[\\[\\] ]", ""));
    }

    private static List<Long> generateFibonacciSeries(int termCount) {
        return Stream.iterate(new long[]{0L, 1L},
                pair -> new long[]{pair[1], pair[0] + pair[1]})
            .limit(termCount)
            .map(pair -> pair[0])
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
    }
}
Java 7 equivalent

public class GenerateFibonacciSeriesJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {

        System.out.println(generateFibonacciSeries(termCount).toString().replaceAll("[\\[\\] ]", ""));
    }

    private static List<Long> generateFibonacciSeries(int termCount) {
        List<Long> fibonacciNumbers = new ArrayList<Long>();
        long first = 0L, second = 1L;
        for (int i = 0; i < termCount; i++) {
            fibonacciNumbers.add(first);
            long next = first + second;
            first = second;
            second = next;
        }
        return fibonacciNumbers;
    }
}

Java 8 solution
import java.util.stream.LongStream;

public class CalculateFactorialJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 5;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + calculateFactorial(number));
    }

    private static long calculateFactorial(int number) {
        return LongStream.rangeClosed(1, number).reduce(1L, (left, right) -> left * right);
    }

        for (int multiplier = 2; multiplier <= number; multiplier++) {

Q135Numbers

Check Armstrong number

Implement the mathematical operation and validate the input domain.

Complexity: O(d) time; O(d) string storage
Sample input / test data
int n = 153;
Expected output
153 -> true
Java 8 solution
public class CheckArmstrongNumberJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 153;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + isArmstrongNumber(number));
    }

    private static boolean isArmstrongNumber(int number) {
        if (number < 0) return false;
        String numberText = String.valueOf(number);
        int digitPowerSum = numberText.chars()
            .map(character -> character - '0')
            .map(digit -> (int) Math.pow(digit, numberText.length()))
            .sum();
        return digitPowerSum == number;
    }
}
Java 7 equivalent
public class CheckArmstrongNumberJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 153;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + isArmstrongNumber(number));
    }

    private static boolean isArmstrongNumber(int number) {
        if (number < 0) return false;
        String numberText = String.valueOf(number);
        int digitPowerSum = 0;
        for (char character : numberText.toCharArray()) {
            digitPowerSum += (int) Math.pow(character - '0', numberText.length());
        }
        return digitPowerSum == number;
    }
}
Explanation and edge cases

How to reason about it: Identify the input size, the data structure that supports the required operation, and the invariant maintained during traversal. Check numeric palindrome

Implement the mathematical operation and validate the input domain.

Complexity: O(d) time; O(d) space
Sample input / test data
int n = 121;
Expected output
121 -> true
Java 8 solution
public class CheckNumericPalindromeJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 121;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + isNumericPalindrome(number));
    }

    private static boolean isNumericPalindrome(int number) {
        if (number < 0) return false;
        String numberText = String.valueOf(number);
        return numberText.equals(new StringBuilder(numberText).reverse().toString());
    }
}
Java 7 equivalent
public class CheckNumericPalindromeJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 121;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + isNumericPalindrome(number));
    }

    private static boolean isNumericPalindrome(int number) {
        if (number < 0) return false;
        String numberText = String.valueOf(number);
        for (int left = 0, right = numberText.length() - 1; left < right; left++, right--) {
            if (numberText.charAt(left) != numberText.charAt(right)) return false;
        }
        return true;
    }
}

Q137Numbers

Calculate sum of digits

Implement the mathematical operation and validate the input domain.

Complexity: O(d) time; O(1) extra
Sample input / test data
int n = 123;
Expected output
123 -> 6
Java 8 solution
public class CalculateSumOfDigitsJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 123;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + calculateSumOfDigits(number));
    }

    private static int calculateSumOfDigits(int number) {
        return String.valueOf(Math.abs((long) number)).chars()
            .map(character -> character - '0')
            .sum();
    }
}
Java 7 equivalent
public class CalculateSumOfDigitsJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 123;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + calculateSumOfDigits(number));
    }

    private static int calculateSumOfDigits(int number) {
        long remaining = Math.abs((long) number);
        int digitSum = 0;
        while (remaining > 0) {
            digitSum += (int) (remaining % 10);
            remaining /= 10;
        }
        return digitSum;
    }
}

Java 8 solution
public class CalculateProductOfDigitsJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 234;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + calculateProductOfDigits(number));
    }

    private static int calculateProductOfDigits(int number) {

Java 8 solution
import java.util.*; import java.util.stream.*;

public class FindSecondLargestDistinctDigitJava8 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 987;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + findSecondLargestDistinctDigit(number));
    }

    private static int findSecondLargestDistinctDigit(int number) {
        return String.valueOf(Math.abs((long) number)).chars()
            .map(character -> character - '0')
            .distinct()
            .boxed()
            .sorted(Comparator.reverseOrder())
            .skip(1)
            .findFirst()
            .orElse(-1);
    }
}
Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;

public class FindSecondLargestDistinctDigitJava7 {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 987;
        System.out.println(number + " -> " + findSecondLargestDistinctDigit(number));
    }

    private static int findSecondLargestDistinctDigit(int number) {
        Set<Integer> uniqueDigits = new TreeSet<Integer>(Collections.reverseOrder());
        for (char character : String.valueOf(Math.abs((long) number)).toCharArray()) {
            uniqueDigits.add(character - '0');
        }
        if (uniqueDigits.size() < 2) return -1;
        Iterator<Integer> iterator = uniqueDigits.iterator();
        iterator.next();
        return iterator.next();
    }
}

Q142NumbersMedium

Reverse an integer with 32-bit overflow handling

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(log10 |n|) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
int n = 123;
Expected output
123 -> 321
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class ReverseInteger32BitOverflowHandlingJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 123;
        System.out.println(n + " -> " + reverse(n));
    }

    static int reverse(int n) {
        long result = 0;
        int value = n;
        while (value != 0) {
            result = result * 10 + value % 10;
            if (result > Integer.MAX_VALUE || result < Integer.MIN_VALUE) return 0;
            value /= 10;
        }
        return (int) result;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent

import java.math.*;

public class ReverseInteger32BitOverflowHandlingJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 123;
        System.out.println(n + " -> " + reverse(n));
    }

    static int reverse(int n) {
        long result = 0;
        int value = n;
        while (value != 0) {
            result = result * 10 + value % 10;
            if (result > Integer.MAX_VALUE || result < Integer.MIN_VALUE) return 0;
            value /= 10;
        }
        return (int) result;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Take the last digit with remainder, append it to the result, then remove it from the input with integer division. A long accumulator detects overflow before the final cast.

Edge cases: Zero, negative input, trailing zeroes, Integer.MIN_VALUE and reversed values outside the int range.

Interview follow-up: Why is the accumulator long? What should the method return on overflow? Compare reversing through String conversion.

Complexity: O(log10 |n|) time; O(1) space

Q143NumbersEasy

Count digits without converting the number to a String

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(d) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
long n = -1200L;
Expected output
-1200 -> 4 digits
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CountDigitsWithoutConvertingNumberToStringJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long n = -1200L;        System.out.println(n + " -> " + countDigits(n) + " digits");
    }

    static int countDigits(long n) {
        if (n == 0) return 1;
        int count = 0;
        long value = n;
        while (value != 0) {
            count++;
            value /= 10;
        }
        return count;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CountDigitsWithoutConvertingNumberToStringJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long n = -1200L;
        System.out.println(n + " -> " + countDigits(n) + " digits");
    }

    static int countDigits(long n) {
        if (n == 0) return 1;
        int count = 0;
        long value = n;
        while (value != 0) {
            count++;
            value /= 10;
        }
        return count;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Repeatedly divide the value by ten. Every division removes one decimal digit. Zero is a special case because the loop would otherwise run zero times.

Edge cases: Zero has one digit; the minus sign is not counted; Long.MIN_VALUE is safe because the method never calls Math.abs.

Interview follow-up: How would you count digits in another base? Why is Math.abs(Long.MIN_VALUE) problematic?

Complexity: O(d) time; O(1) space

Q145NumbersEasy

Check whether a number is a Happy Number

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(log n) expected work per visited value; O(k) space for seen values
Sample input / test data
int n = 19;
Expected output
19 -> true
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CheckWhetherNumberIsHappyNumberJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 19;
        System.out.println(n + " -> " + isHappy(n));
    }

    static boolean isHappy(int n) {
        if (n <= 0) return false;
        Set<Integer> seen = new HashSet<Integer>();
        int value = n;
        while (value != 1 && seen.add(value)) {
            int sum = 0;
            while (value > 0) {
                int digit = value % 10;
                sum += digit * digit;
                value /= 10;
            }
            value = sum;
        }
        return value == 1;
    }
}

import java.math.*;

Interview follow-up: Can Floyd cycle detection remove the HashSet? Why must the process terminate?

Complexity: O(log n) expected work per visited value; O(k) space for seen values

Q150NumbersEasy

Find the GCD of two numbers using the Euclidean algorithm

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(log min(a,b)) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
long a = 48, b = 18;
Expected output

Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class FindGCDOfTwoNumbersEuclideanAlgorithmJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long a = 48, b = 18;
        System.out.println("GCD(" + a + ", " + b + ") = " + gcd(a, b));
    }

    static long gcd(long a, long b) {
        a = Math.abs(a);
        b = Math.abs(b);
        while (b != 0) {
            long remainder = a % b;
            a = b;
            b = remainder;
        }
        return a;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent

import java.math.*;

    }

        a = Math.abs(a);

        while (b != 0) {
            long remainder = a % b;
            a = b;
            b = remainder;
        }

}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Replace the pair (a,b) with (b,a mod b). The GCD is unchanged by this transformation, and the remainder decreases until it becomes zero.

Edge cases: GCD(a,0)=|a|; GCD(0,0) is defined here as zero. Long.MIN_VALUE needs a BigInteger-based contract if supported.

Interview follow-up: Why does the Euclidean algorithm work? What is its worst-case input pattern?

Q151NumbersEasy

Find the LCM of two numbers without overflowing intermediate multiplication

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(log min(a,b)) arithmetic steps; O(1) space excluding BigInteger storage
Sample input / test data
long a = 12, b = 18;
Expected output
LCM(12, 18) = 36
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class FindLCMOfTwoNumbersWithoutOverflowingIntermediateMultiplicationJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long a = 12, b = 18;
        System.out.println("LCM(" + a + ", " + b + ") = " + lcm(a, b));
    }

    static BigInteger lcm(long a, long b) {
        if (a == 0 || b == 0) return BigInteger.ZERO;
        BigInteger x = BigInteger.valueOf(a).abs();
        BigInteger y = BigInteger.valueOf(b).abs();
        return x.divide(x.gcd(y)).multiply(y);
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class FindLCMOfTwoNumbersWithoutOverflowingIntermediateMultiplicationJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long a = 12, b = 18;
        System.out.println("LCM(" + a + ", " + b + ") = " + lcm(a, b));
    }

    static BigInteger lcm(long a, long b) {
        if (a == 0 || b == 0) return BigInteger.ZERO;
        BigInteger x = BigInteger.valueOf(a).abs();
        BigInteger y = BigInteger.valueOf(b).abs();
        return x.divide(x.gcd(y)).multiply(y);
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Use LCM(a,b)=|a/gcd(a,b) × b|. BigInteger keeps the result exact even when it exceeds the long range; dividing before multiplying also reduces intermediate size.

Edge cases: Either input zero gives zero. Negative inputs produce a non-negative LCM.

Interview follow-up: Why should division happen before multiplication? When would a long return type be insufficient?

Complexity: O(log min(a,b)) arithmetic steps; O(1) space excluding BigInteger storage

Q152NumbersMedium

Find the GCD of an array of numbers

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(n log M) time; O(1) auxiliary space
Sample input / test data

Expected output
GCD of array = 12
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class FindGCDOfArrayOfNumbersJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long[] nums = {24, 36, 60};
        System.out.println("GCD of array = " + gcdArray(nums));
    }

    static long gcdArray(long[] nums) {
        if (nums.length == 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("array must not be empty");
        long result = 0;
        for (long value : nums) result = gcd(result, value);
        return result;
    }

    static long gcd(long a, long b) {
        a = Math.abs(a); b = Math.abs(b);
        while (b != 0) { long t = a % b; a = b; b = t; }
        return a;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent

import java.math.*;

public class FindGCDOfArrayOfNumbersJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {

    }

    static long gcdArray(long[] nums) {
        if (nums.length == 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("array must not be empty");
        long result = 0;
        for (long value : nums) result = gcd(result, value);
        return result;
    }

    static long gcd(long a, long b) {
        a = Math.abs(a); b = Math.abs(b);
        while (b != 0) { long t = a % b; a = b; b = t; }
        return a;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Fold the Euclidean GCD across the array. Start at zero because gcd(0,x)=|x|, then combine each next value with the accumulated result.

Edge cases: An empty array is rejected. Zeros and negative values are supported except Long.MIN_VALUE under the long-only absolute-value contract.

Interview follow-up: Can the fold stop early when the running GCD becomes one?

Complexity: O(n log M) time; O(1) auxiliary space

Q153NumbersMedium

Reduce a fraction to its simplest form

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(log min(|n|,|d|)) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
long numerator = 42, denominator = 56;
Expected output
42/56 = 3/4
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class ReduceFractionToItsSimplestFormJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long numerator = 42, denominator = 56;
        System.out.println(numerator + "/" + denominator + " = " + simplify(numerator, denominator));
    }

    static String simplify(long numerator, long denominator) {
        if (denominator == 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("denominator must not be zero");
        BigInteger n = BigInteger.valueOf(numerator);
        BigInteger d = BigInteger.valueOf(denominator);
        BigInteger gcd = n.abs().gcd(d.abs());
        n = n.divide(gcd); d = d.divide(gcd);
        if (d.signum() < 0) { n = n.negate(); d = d.negate(); }
        return n + "/" + d;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class ReduceFractionToItsSimplestFormJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long numerator = 42, denominator = 56;
        System.out.println(numerator + "/" + denominator + " = " + simplify(numerator, denominator));
    }

    static String simplify(long numerator, long denominator) {
        if (denominator == 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("denominator must not be zero");
        BigInteger n = BigInteger.valueOf(numerator);
        BigInteger d = BigInteger.valueOf(denominator);
        BigInteger gcd = n.abs().gcd(d.abs());
        n = n.divide(gcd); d = d.divide(gcd);
        if (d.signum() < 0) { n = n.negate(); d = d.negate(); }
        return n + "/" + d;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor. Move any negative sign to the numerator so the denominator is positive.

Edge cases: Zero denominator is invalid. Zero numerator reduces to 0/1. BigInteger handles Long.MIN_VALUE safely.

Interview follow-up: Why normalize the denominator sign? How would you add two reduced fractions without overflow?

Complexity: O(log min(|n|,|d|)) time; O(1) space

Q154NumbersEasy

Generate all divisors of a number in sorted order

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Sample input / test data

Expected output

Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class GenerateAllDivisorsOfNumberInSortedOrderJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 36;
        System.out.println("Divisors of " + n + " = " + divisors(n));
    }

    static List<Integer> divisors(int n) {
        if (n <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("n must be positive");
        List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
        for (int i = 1; (long) i * i <= n; i++) {
            if (n % i == 0) {
                result.add(i);
                if (i != n / i) result.add(n / i);
            }
        }
        Collections.sort(result);
        return result;
    }
}

Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CalculateSumOfProperDivisorsJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 28;
        System.out.println("Sum of proper divisors of " + n + " = " + sumProperDivisors(n));
    }

    static long sumProperDivisors(int n) {
        if (n <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("n must be positive");
        if (n == 1) return 0;

        for (int i = 2; (long) i * i <= n; i++) {
            if (n % i == 0) {

                if (pair != i) sum += pair;
            }
        }
        return sum;
    }
}

                sum += i;
                if (i != n / i) sum += n / i;
            }
        }
        return sum == n;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: A perfect number equals the sum of its positive proper divisors. Add divisor pairs only up to the square root and omit the number itself.

Edge cases: Numbers less than or equal to one are not perfect. Test perfect squares to ensure the square root is not counted twice.

Interview follow-up: What is an abundant number? What is a deficient number?

Complexity: O(sqrt n) time; O(1) space

Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class FindPrimeFactorizationFactorFrequenciesJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 360;
        System.out.println("Prime factorization of " + n + " = " + factorize(n));
    }

    static Map<Integer, Integer> factorize(int n) {
        if (n < 2) throw new IllegalArgumentException("n must be at least 2");
        Map<Integer, Integer> factors = new TreeMap<Integer, Integer>();
        for (int p = 2; (long) p * p <= n; p++) {
            while (n % p == 0) {
                Integer old = factors.get(p);
                factors.put(p, old == null ? 1 : old + 1);
                n /= p;
            }
        }
        if (n > 1) factors.put(n, 1);
        return factors;
    }
}

    static long sumPrimes(int low, int high) {
        if (high < low) throw new IllegalArgumentException("high must be >= low");
        if (high < 2) return 0;
