        for (int p = 2; (long) p * p <= high; p++) {
            if (!composite[p]) for (int j = p * p; j <= high; j += p) composite[j] = true;

public class CheckWhetherNumberCanBeExpressedAsSumOfTwoPrimesJava8 {

Q165NumbersHard

Generate primes in a large range using a Segmented Sieve

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O((R-L+1) log log R + sqrt(R) log log R) time; O(sqrt R + R-L) space
Sample input / test data
int low = 100, high = 130;
Expected output
Primes from 100 to 130 = [101, 103, 107, 109, 113, 127]
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class GeneratePrimesInLargeRangeSegmentedSieveJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int low = 100, high = 130;
        System.out.println("Primes from " + low + " to " + high + " = " + segmentedSieve(low, high));
    }

    static List<Integer> segmentedSieve(int low, int high) {
        if (high < low) throw new IllegalArgumentException("high must be >= low");
        List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
        if (high < 2) return result;
        int limit = (int) Math.sqrt(high);
        boolean[] baseComposite = new boolean[limit + 1];
        List<Integer> basePrimes = new ArrayList<Integer>();
        for (int p = 2; p <= limit; p++) {
            if (!baseComposite[p]) {
                basePrimes.add(p);
                if ((long) p * p <= limit)
                    for (int j = p * p; j <= limit; j += p) baseComposite[j] = true;
            }
        }
        int start = Math.max(low, 2);
        boolean[] composite = new boolean[high - start + 1];
        for (int p : basePrimes) {
            long first = Math.max((long) p * p, ((start + (long) p - 1) / p) * p);
            for (long j = first; j <= high; j += p) composite[(int) (j - start)] = true;
        }
        for (int i = 0; i < composite.length; i++) if (!composite[i]) result.add(start + i);
        return result;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent

import java.math.*;

public class GeneratePrimesInLargeRangeSegmentedSieveJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int low = 100, high = 130;
        System.out.println("Primes from " + low + " to " + high + " = " + segmentedSieve(low, high));
    }

    static List<Integer> segmentedSieve(int low, int high) {
        if (high < low) throw new IllegalArgumentException("high must be >= low");
        List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
        if (high < 2) return result;
        int limit = (int) Math.sqrt(high);
        boolean[] baseComposite = new boolean[limit + 1];
        List<Integer> basePrimes = new ArrayList<Integer>();
        for (int p = 2; p <= limit; p++) {
            if (!baseComposite[p]) {
                basePrimes.add(p);
                if ((long) p * p <= limit)
                    for (int j = p * p; j <= limit; j += p) baseComposite[j] = true;
            }
        }
        int start = Math.max(low, 2);
        boolean[] composite = new boolean[high - start + 1];
        for (int p : basePrimes) {
            long first = Math.max((long) p * p, ((start + (long) p - 1) / p) * p);
            for (long j = first; j <= high; j += p) composite[(int) (j - start)] = true;
        }
        for (int i = 0; i < composite.length; i++) if (!composite[i]) result.add(start + i);
        return result;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: First generate primes up to sqrt(high). Use them to mark composites only inside the requested interval. This avoids allocating an array from zero to high.

Edge cases: The interval is inclusive. Negative low values are safely clamped to two. The implementation assumes high is a practical non-negative int because the segment itself is stored in an array.

Interview follow-up: Why does each base prime start marking at max(p squared, first multiple in range)?

Complexity: O((R-L+1) log log R + sqrt(R) log log R) time; O(sqrt R + R-L) space

Q166NumbersMedium

Calculate X raised to power N using fast exponentiation

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(log |n|) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
double x = 2.0; int n = 10;
Expected output

Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CalculateXRaisedToPowerNFastExponentiationJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        double x = 2.0;
        int n = 10;
        System.out.println(x + " ^ " + n + " = " + power(x, n));
    }

    static double power(double x, int n) {
        long exponent = n;
        if (exponent < 0) { x = 1.0 / x; exponent = -exponent; }
        double result = 1.0;
        while (exponent > 0) {
            if ((exponent & 1L) == 1L) result *= x;
            x *= x;
            exponent >>= 1;
        }
        return result;
    }
}

Interview follow-up: Why is this faster than multiplying x by itself n times? What floating-point precision issues can occur?

Complexity: O(log |n|) time; O(1) space

Q167NumbersMedium

Calculate modular exponentiation efficiently

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(log exponent) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
long base = 2, exponent = 10, mod = 1000;
Expected output
2^10 mod 1000 = 24
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CalculateModularExponentiationEfficientlyJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long base = 2, exponent = 10, mod = 1000;
        System.out.println(base + "^" + exponent + " mod " + mod + " = " + modPow(base, exponent, mod));
    }

    static long modPow(long base, long exponent, long mod) {
        if (exponent < 0 || mod <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("exponent must be non-negative and mod positive");
        long result = 1 % mod;
        base = ((base % mod) + mod) % mod;
        while (exponent > 0) {
            if ((exponent & 1L) == 1L) result = (result * base) % mod;
            base = (base * base) % mod;
            exponent >>= 1;
        }
        return result;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CalculateModularExponentiationEfficientlyJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long base = 2, exponent = 10, mod = 1000;
        System.out.println(base + "^" + exponent + " mod " + mod + " = " + modPow(base, exponent, mod));
    }

    static long modPow(long base, long exponent, long mod) {
        if (exponent < 0 || mod <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("exponent must be non-negative and mod positive");
        long result = 1 % mod;
        base = ((base % mod) + mod) % mod;
        while (exponent > 0) {
            if ((exponent & 1L) == 1L) result = (result * base) % mod;
            base = (base * base) % mod;
            exponent >>= 1;
        }
        return result;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Repeatedly square the base modulo mod and halve the exponent. Modular reduction keeps intermediate values bounded for the stated constraints.

Edge cases: Requires mod greater than zero and exponent non-negative. This long implementation assumes mod is small enough that products of reduced operands fit in long; use BigInteger for arbitrary moduli.

Interview follow-up: How would you support a modulus large enough for long multiplication to overflow?

Complexity: O(log exponent) time; O(1) space

Q168NumbersMedium

Find the integer square root without using Math.sqrt

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(log n) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
int n = 26;
Expected output
Integer square root of 26 = 5
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class FindIntegerSquareRootWithoutMathSqrtJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 26;
        System.out.println("Integer square root of " + n + " = " + integerSqrt(n));
    }

    static int integerSqrt(int n) {
        if (n < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("n must be non-negative");
        int low = 0, high = n, answer = 0;
        while (low <= high) {
            int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
            long square = (long) mid * mid;
            if (square <= n) { answer = mid; low = mid + 1; }
            else high = mid - 1;
        }
        return answer;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class FindIntegerSquareRootWithoutMathSqrtJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 26;
        System.out.println("Integer square root of " + n + " = " + integerSqrt(n));
    }

    static int integerSqrt(int n) {
        if (n < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("n must be non-negative");
        int low = 0, high = n, answer = 0;
        while (low <= high) {
            int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
            long square = (long) mid * mid;
            if (square <= n) { answer = mid; low = mid + 1; }
            else high = mid - 1;
        }
        return answer;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Binary search for the greatest integer whose square is no greater than n. The multiplication is promoted to long to avoid int overflow.

Edge cases: Negative input is rejected. Zero returns zero; perfect squares return their exact root.

Interview follow-up: Why is binary search valid here? What does integer square root return for 26?

Complexity: O(log n) time; O(1) space

Complete Java 8 program

public class FindIntegerNthRootOfNumberJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long x = 64;
        int n = 3;
        System.out.println("Integer " + n + "rd root of " + x + " = " + integerRoot(x, n));
    }

    static long integerRoot(long x, int n) {
        if (x < 0 || n <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("x must be non-negative and n positive");
        long low = 0, high = x, answer = 0;
        while (low <= high) {
            long mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
            int comparison = comparePower(mid, n, x);
            if (comparison <= 0) { answer = mid; low = mid + 1; }
            else high = mid - 1;
        }
        return answer;
    }

    static int comparePower(long base, int exponent, long limit) {
        long result = 1;
        for (int i = 0; i < exponent; i++) {
            if (base != 0 && result > limit / base) return 1;
            result *= base;
        }
        return Long.compare(result, limit);
    }
}

Q170NumbersMedium

Divide two integers without multiplication, division or modulo

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(32) time; O(1) space for 32-bit integers
Sample input / test data
int dividend = 43, divisor = -5;
Expected output
43 / -5 = -8
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class DivideTwoIntegersWithoutMultiplicationDivisionOrModuloJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int dividend = 43, divisor = -5;
        System.out.println(dividend + " / " + divisor + " = " + divide(dividend, divisor));
    }

    static int divide(int dividend, int divisor) {
        if (divisor == 0) throw new ArithmeticException("division by zero");
        if (dividend == Integer.MIN_VALUE && divisor == -1) return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        long a = Math.abs((long) dividend);
        long b = Math.abs((long) divisor);
        long quotient = 0;
        for (int bit = 31; bit >= 0; bit--) {
            if ((a >> bit) >= b) {
                a -= b << bit;
                quotient |= 1L << bit;
            }
        }
        if ((dividend < 0) ^ (divisor < 0)) quotient = -quotient;
        return (int) quotient;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent

import java.math.*;

    }

        if (dividend == Integer.MIN_VALUE && divisor == -1) return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        long a = Math.abs((long) dividend);
        long b = Math.abs((long) divisor);
        long quotient = 0;
        for (int bit = 31; bit >= 0; bit--) {
            if ((a >> bit) >= b) {
                a -= b << bit;
                quotient |= 1L << bit;
            }
        }
        if ((dividend < 0) ^ (divisor < 0)) quotient = -quotient;
        return (int) quotient;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Use shifted copies of the divisor to subtract the largest possible power-of-two multiple from the dividend. Set the corresponding quotient bit, then apply the sign.

Edge cases: Division by zero throws. Integer.MIN_VALUE / -1 is clamped to Integer.MAX_VALUE to avoid overflow, matching common interview problem requirements. Division truncates toward zero.

Interview follow-up: Why convert both inputs to long before taking absolute values?

Complexity: O(32) time; O(1) space for 32-bit integers

Convert an integer to any base from 2 through 36 without built-in conversion methods

Sample input / test data

Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class ConvertIntegerToAnyBase2Through36WithoutBuiltInConversionMethodsJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int number = 255, base = 16;
        System.out.println(number + " in base " + base + " = " + toBase(number, base));
    }

    static String toBase(int number, int base) {
        if (base < 2 || base > 36) throw new IllegalArgumentException("base must be between 2 and 36");
        if (number == 0) return "0";
        long value = number;
        boolean negative = value < 0;
        if (negative) value = -value;
        String digits = "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ";
        StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
        while (value > 0) {
            int remainder = (int) (value % base);
            result.append(digits.charAt(remainder));
            value /= base;
        }
        if (negative) result.append('-');
        return result.reverse().toString();
    }
}

Complexity: O(log_base n) time; O(log_base n) output space

Q172NumbersMedium

Calculate N choose R (binomial coefficient)

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(r) BigInteger multiplications; O(1) count of BigInteger variables
Sample input / test data
int n = 5, r = 2;
Expected output
5C2 = 10
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CalculateNChooseRJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 5, r = 2;
        System.out.println(n + "C" + r + " = " + nCr(n, r));
    }

    static BigInteger nCr(int n, int r) {
        if (n < 0 || r < 0 || r > n) throw new IllegalArgumentException("require n >= 0 and 0 <= r <= n");
        r = Math.min(r, n - r);
        BigInteger result = BigInteger.ONE;
        for (int i = 1; i <= r; i++) {
            result = result.multiply(BigInteger.valueOf(n - r + i)).divide(BigInteger.valueOf(i));
        }
        return result;
    }
}

Edge cases: C(n,0)=C(n,n)=1. Values outside 0<=r<=n are rejected.

Interview follow-up: Why can symmetry reduce the iteration count? How does Pascal dynamic programming compare?

Complexity: O(r) BigInteger multiplications; O(1) count of BigInteger variables

Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class SolveJosephusProblemJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 7, k = 3;
        System.out.println("Josephus survivor (1-based) = " + josephus(n, k));
    }

    static int josephus(int n, int k) {
        if (n <= 0 || k <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("n and k must be positive");
        long survivor = 0;
        for (int size = 1; size <= n; size++) survivor = (survivor + k) % size;
        return (int) survivor + 1;
    }
}

Q176NumbersMedium

Count values divisible by A or B up to N using inclusion-exclusion

Complexity: O(log min(a,b)) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data

Expected output
Count from 1 to 20 divisible by 3 or 5 = 9
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CountValuesDivisibleByOrBUpToNInclusionExclusionJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long n = 20, a = 3, b = 5;
        System.out.println("Count from 1 to " + n + " divisible by " + a + " or " + b + " = " + count(n, a, b));
    }

    static long count(long n, long a, long b) {
        if (n < 0 || a <= 0 || b <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("n must be non-negative and divisors positive");
        long gcd = gcd(a, b);
        BigInteger lcm = BigInteger.valueOf(a / gcd).multiply(BigInteger.valueOf(b));
        BigInteger limit = BigInteger.valueOf(n);
        long both = limit.divide(lcm).longValue();
        return n / a + n / b - both;
    }

    static long gcd(long a, long b) {
        while (b != 0) { long t = a % b; a = b; b = t; }
        return a;
    }
}

Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class AddTwoFractionsAndReduceResultJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long a = 1, b = 6, c = 1, d = 4;
        System.out.println(a + "/" + b + " + " + c + "/" + d + " = " + addFractions(a, b, c, d));
    }

    static String addFractions(long a, long b, long c, long d) {
        if (b == 0 || d == 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("denominators must not be zero");
        BigInteger A = BigInteger.valueOf(a), B = BigInteger.valueOf(b);
        BigInteger C = BigInteger.valueOf(c), D = BigInteger.valueOf(d);
        BigInteger numerator = A.multiply(D).add(C.multiply(B));
        BigInteger denominator = B.multiply(D);
        BigInteger gcd = numerator.abs().gcd(denominator.abs());
        numerator = numerator.divide(gcd); denominator = denominator.divide(gcd);
        if (denominator.signum() < 0) { numerator = numerator.negate(); denominator = denominator.negate(); }
        return numerator + "/" + denominator;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent

import java.math.*;

    }

    static String addFractions(long a, long b, long c, long d) {
        if (b == 0 || d == 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("denominators must not be zero");
        BigInteger A = BigInteger.valueOf(a), B = BigInteger.valueOf(b);
        BigInteger C = BigInteger.valueOf(c), D = BigInteger.valueOf(d);

        return numerator + "/" + denominator;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Use a common denominator: a/b+c/d=(ad+bc)/(bd). Divide both terms by their GCD and normalize the denominator to be positive.

Edge cases: Zero denominator is rejected. BigInteger avoids intermediate overflow. A zero result is normalized to 0/1.

Interview follow-up: How can you reduce intermediate growth by using the GCD of the two denominators first?

Complexity: O(log min denominator) time; O(1) space apart from BigInteger values

Q178NumbersHard

Find the modular multiplicative inverse using Extended Euclid

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(log m) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
long a = 3, mod = 11;
Expected output
Modular inverse of 3 modulo 11 = 4
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class FindModularMultiplicativeInverseExtendedEuclidJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        long a = 3, mod = 11;
        System.out.println("Modular inverse of " + a + " modulo " + mod + " = " + modInverse(a, mod));
    }

    static long modInverse(long a, long mod) {
        if (mod <= 1) throw new IllegalArgumentException("modulus must be greater than one");
        long oldR = a, r = mod, oldS = 1, s = 0;
        while (r != 0) {
            long q = oldR / r;
            long temp = oldR - q * r; oldR = r; r = temp;
            temp = oldS - q * s; oldS = s; s = temp;
        }
        if (Math.abs(oldR) != 1) return -1;
        return ((oldS % mod) + mod) % mod;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent

import java.math.*;

public class FindModularMultiplicativeInverseExtendedEuclidJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {

        System.out.println("Modular inverse of " + a + " modulo " + mod + " = " + modInverse(a, mod));
    }

    static long modInverse(long a, long mod) {
        if (mod <= 1) throw new IllegalArgumentException("modulus must be greater than one");
        long oldR = a, r = mod, oldS = 1, s = 0;
        while (r != 0) {
            long q = oldR / r;
            long temp = oldR - q * r; oldR = r; r = temp;
            temp = oldS - q * s; oldS = s; s = temp;
        }
        if (Math.abs(oldR) != 1) return -1;
        return ((oldS % mod) + mod) % mod;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Extended Euclid computes coefficients x and y such that ax+my=gcd(a,m). When the GCD is one, x modulo m is the multiplicative inverse.

Edge cases: An inverse exists only when gcd(a,m)=1. This long implementation assumes intermediate coefficient products remain within long; use BigInteger for unrestricted inputs.

Interview follow-up: Why does an inverse not exist when the GCD is not one? How is this used in modular division?

Complexity: O(log m) time; O(1) space

import java.math.*;

public class CheckWhetherNumberIsPowerOfFourJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 64;
        System.out.println(n + " -> " + isPowerOfFour(n));
    }

    static boolean isPowerOfFour(int n) {
        return n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0 && (n & 0x55555555) != 0;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: A power of four is a power of two whose single set bit occupies an even zero-based bit position. The mask 0x55555555 selects those positions.

Edge cases: Zero and negative values return false. The mask assumes a 32-bit int representation.

Interview follow-up: Why does the mask distinguish powers of four from powers of two?

Complexity: O(1) time; O(1) space

Q180NumbersEasy

Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CountSetBitsInIntegerJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 29;
        System.out.println("Set bits in " + n + " = " + countSetBits(n));
    }

Q181NumbersEasy

Calculate Hamming distance between two integers

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(number of differing bits) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
int a = 1, b = 4;
Expected output
Hamming distance between 1 and 4 = 2
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CalculateHammingDistanceBetweenTwoIntegersJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int a = 1, b = 4;
        System.out.println("Hamming distance between " + a + " and " + b + " = " + hammingDistance(a, b));
    }

    static int hammingDistance(int a, int b) {
        int value = a ^ b;
        int count = 0;
        while (value != 0) { value &= value - 1; count++; }
        return count;
    }
}

        int value = a ^ b;
        int count = 0;
        while (value != 0) { value &= value - 1; count++; }

}

Q182NumbersMedium

Reverse the bits of a 32-bit integer

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(32) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
int n = 43261596;
Expected output
Reverse bits of 43261596 = 964176192
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class ReverseBitsOf32BitIntegerJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 43261596;
        System.out.println("Reverse bits of " + n + " = " + reverseBits(n));
    }

    static int reverseBits(int n) {
        int result = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) {
            result = (result << 1) | (n & 1);
            n >>>= 1;
        }
        return result;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class ReverseBitsOf32BitIntegerJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 43261596;
        System.out.println("Reverse bits of " + n + " = " + reverseBits(n));
    }

    static int reverseBits(int n) {
        int result = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) {
            result = (result << 1) | (n & 1);
            n >>>= 1;
        }
        return result;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: Repeat exactly 32 times: shift the result left and append the current least significant bit of the input. Use unsigned right shift so sign extension does not occur.

Edge cases: All 32 bits are processed, including leading zeroes. The returned int may be negative if its high bit becomes one.

Interview follow-up: Why must the loop execute exactly 32 times? What is the difference between >> and >>>?

Complexity: O(32) time; O(1) space

Q183NumbersMedium

Add two integers without using plus or minus

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(32) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
int a = 15, b = 27;
Expected output
15 + 27 = 42
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class AddTwoIntegersWithoutPlusOrMinusJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int a = 15, b = 27;
        System.out.println(a + " + " + b + " = " + addWithoutPlus(a, b));
    }

    static int addWithoutPlus(int a, int b) {
        while (b != 0) {
            int carry = (a & b) << 1;
            a = a ^ b;
            b = carry;
        }
        return a;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class AddTwoIntegersWithoutPlusOrMinusJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int a = 15, b = 27;
        System.out.println(a + " + " + b + " = " + addWithoutPlus(a, b));
    }

    static int addWithoutPlus(int a, int b) {
        while (b != 0) {
            int carry = (a & b) << 1;
            a = a ^ b;
            b = carry;
        }
        return a;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: XOR computes the sum bits without carry. AND identifies carry positions; shifting the carry left aligns it for the next iteration. Stop when no carry remains.

Edge cases: Java int arithmetic wraps on 32-bit overflow, matching normal int addition semantics. The method terminates within a bounded number of bit operations.

Interview follow-up: How would subtraction be implemented using bitwise operations?

Complexity: O(32) time; O(1) space

Q184NumbersEasy

Find XOR of all numbers from 1 to N

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(1) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
int n = 10;
Expected output
XOR from 1 to 10 = 11
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class FindXOROfAllNumbers1ToNJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 10;
        System.out.println("XOR from 1 to " + n + " = " + xorOneToN(n));
    }

    static int xorOneToN(int n) {
        if (n < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("n must be non-negative");
        switch (n & 3) {
            case 0: return n;
            case 1: return 1;
            case 2: return n + 1;
            default: return 0;
        }
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent

import java.math.*;

public class FindXOROfAllNumbers1ToNJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 10;
        System.out.println("XOR from 1 to " + n + " = " + xorOneToN(n));
    }

    static int xorOneToN(int n) {
        if (n < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("n must be non-negative");
        switch (n & 3) {
            case 0: return n;
            case 1: return 1;
            case 2: return n + 1;
            default: return 0;
        }
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: The XOR pattern repeats every four values: n, 1, n+1, 0 according to n modulo four. Select the result directly without iterating.

Edge cases: n must be non-negative. For Integer.MAX_VALUE, the n+1 branch cannot occur because that value has remainder three.

Interview follow-up: Why does the XOR prefix pattern repeat every four values?

Complexity: O(1) time; O(1) space

Q185NumbersMedium

Count set bits for every number from 0 to N using dynamic programming

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(n) space
Sample input / test data
int n = 5;
Expected output
Set-bit counts from 0 to 5 = [0, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2]
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CountSetBitsForEveryNumber0ToNDynamicProgrammingJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 5;
        System.out.println("Set-bit counts from 0 to " + n + " = " + Arrays.toString(countBits(n)));
    }

    static int[] countBits(int n) {
        if (n < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("n must be non-negative");
        int[] dp = new int[n + 1];
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) dp[i] = dp[i >> 1] + (i & 1);
        return dp;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CountSetBitsForEveryNumber0ToNDynamicProgrammingJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {

        System.out.println("Set-bit counts from 0 to " + n + " = " + Arrays.toString(countBits(n)));
    }

    static int[] countBits(int n) {
        if (n < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("n must be non-negative");
        int[] dp = new int[n + 1];
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) dp[i] = dp[i >> 1] + (i & 1);
        return dp;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: The number of set bits in i equals the set-bit count of i shifted right by one, plus its least significant bit. Previously computed values are reused.

Edge cases: N must be non-negative. The returned array includes the result for zero.

Interview follow-up: Can you derive an alternative recurrence using i & (i-1)?

Complexity: O(n) time; O(n) space

Q186NumbersMedium

Check whether a number has alternating bits

Write a complete program to solve the stated number or mathematics problem. Use the sample values to verify the result.

Complexity: O(1) time; O(1) space for 32-bit integers
Sample input / test data
int n = 10;
Expected output
10 (binary 1010) -> true
Complete Java 8 program
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CheckWhetherNumberHasAlternatingBitsJava8 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 10;
        System.out.println(n + " (binary " + Integer.toBinaryString(n) + ") -> " + hasAlternatingBits(n));
    }

    static boolean hasAlternatingBits(int n) {
        if (n <= 0) return false;
        int changed = n ^ (n >>> 1);
        return (changed & (changed + 1)) == 0;
    }
}
Complete Java 7 equivalent
import java.util.*;
import java.math.*;

public class CheckWhetherNumberHasAlternatingBitsJava7 {
public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 10;
        System.out.println(n + " (binary " + Integer.toBinaryString(n) + ") -> " + hasAlternatingBits(n));
    }

    static boolean hasAlternatingBits(int n) {
        if (n <= 0) return false;
        int changed = n ^ (n >>> 1);
        return (changed & (changed + 1)) == 0;
    }
}
Approach, edge cases and interview follow-ups

Approach: XOR the value with itself shifted right by one. Alternating bits produce a run of consecutive one bits in the changed value; a run of ones satisfies x & (x+1) == 0.

Edge cases: This version requires a positive integer. One is considered to have alternating bits because it has no adjacent equal bit pair.

Interview follow-up: Explain why the XOR operation turns alternating bits into a sequence of ones.

Complexity: O(1) time; O(1) space for 32-bit integers

Q187Stream API

Filter Numbers Greater Than a Given Value

Numbers: [20, 60, 80, 40]; threshold: 50
Expected output

Java 8 – Complete Runnable Program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class FilterNumbersGreaterThanJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(20, 60, 80, 40);
                    int threshold = 50;
            System.out.println(filterNumbersGreaterThan(numbers, threshold));
        }

    private static List<Integer> filterNumbersGreaterThan(List<Integer> numbers, int threshold) {
            return numbers.stream().filter(number -> number > threshold).collect(Collectors.toList());
        }
}
Java 7 – Complete Runnable Equivalent

public class FilterNumbersGreaterThanJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(20, 60, 80, 40);
                    int threshold = 50;
            System.out.println(filterNumbersGreaterThan(numbers, threshold));
        }

    private static List<Integer> filterNumbersGreaterThan(List<Integer> numbers, int threshold) {
            List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
            for (Integer number : numbers) if (number > threshold) result.add(number);
            return result;
        }
}

        }

Q203Stream API

Find the First Non-Repeated Character

Find the first character whose frequency is one, preserving the original character order.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(k) auxiliary space
Sample input / test data
Input string: "swiss"
Expected output
w
Java 8 – Complete Runnable Program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class FindFirstNonRepeatedCharacterJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            String input = "swiss";
            System.out.println(findFirstNonRepeatedCharacter(input));
        }

    private static Character findFirstNonRepeatedCharacter(String input) {
            Map<Character, Long> frequency = input.chars().mapToObj(value -> (char) value).collect(Collectors.groupingBy(character -> character, LinkedHashMap::new, Collectors.counting()));
            return input.chars().mapToObj(value -> (char) value).filter(character -> frequency.get(character) == 1L).findFirst().orElse(null);
        }
}
Java 7 – Complete Runnable Equivalent
import java.util.*;

public class FindFirstNonRepeatedCharacterJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            String input = "swiss";
            System.out.println(findFirstNonRepeatedCharacter(input));
        }

    private static Character findFirstNonRepeatedCharacter(String input) {
            Map<Character, Integer> frequency = new LinkedHashMap<Character, Integer>();
            for (int index = 0; index < input.length(); index++) { char character = input.charAt(index); Integer count = frequency.get(character); frequency.put(character, count == null ? 1 : count + 1); }
            for (int index = 0; index < input.length(); index++) if (frequency.get(input.charAt(index)) == 1) return input.charAt(index);
            return null;
        }
}

        }

            Integer highest = null, secondHighest = null;
            for (Integer number : numbers) { if (highest == null || number > highest) { if (highest == null || !number.equals(highest)) secondHighest = highest; highest = number; } else if (number < highest && (secondHighest == null || number > secondHighest)) secondHighest = number; }

import java.util.*;

public class FindTopNHighestDistinctNumbersJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {            List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(8, 3, 12, 12, 5, 10);
                    int limit = 3;
            System.out.println(findTopNHighestDistinctNumbers(numbers, limit));
        }

    private static List<Integer> findTopNHighestDistinctNumbers(List<Integer> numbers, int limit) {
            if (limit <= 0) return Collections.emptyList();
            Set<Integer> distinct = new HashSet<Integer>(numbers);
            List<Integer> sorted = new ArrayList<Integer>(distinct);

            return new ArrayList<Integer>(sorted.subList(0, Math.min(limit, sorted.size())));
        }
}

            System.out.println(findSecondLongestDistinctString(words));
        }

    private static String findSecondLongestDistinctString(List<String> words) {

Expected output

Java 8 – Complete Runnable Program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;

public class DemonstrateLazyEvaluationJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3);
            System.out.println(demonstrateLazyEvaluation(numbers));
        }

    private static String demonstrateLazyEvaluation(List<Integer> numbers) {
            AtomicInteger processed = new AtomicInteger();
            Stream<Integer> pipeline = numbers.stream().filter(number -> { processed.incrementAndGet(); return number > 1; });
            String before = "Before terminal operation: " + processed.get();
            List<Integer> result = pipeline.collect(Collectors.toList());
            return before + "; Result: " + result + "; Processed: " + processed.get();
        }
}

            int processed = 0; List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
            String before = "Before terminal operation: " + processed;
            for (Integer number : numbers) { processed++; if (number > 1) result.add(number); }

import java.util.*;

public class FindIntersectionOfMultipleListsJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            List<List<Integer>> lists = Arrays.asList(Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3, 4), Arrays.asList(2, 3, 4), Arrays.asList(0, 2, 4));

        }

    private static List<Integer> findIntersectionOfMultipleLists(List<List<Integer>> lists) {
            if (lists.isEmpty()) return Collections.emptyList();

        }

            System.out.println(findIntersectionOfMultipleLists(lists));
        }

    private static List<Integer> findIntersectionOfMultipleLists(List<List<Integer>> lists) {
            if (lists.isEmpty()) return Collections.emptyList();
            List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
            for (Integer number : new LinkedHashSet<Integer>(lists.get(0))) { boolean inEveryList = true; for (int index = 1; index < lists.size(); index++) if (!lists.get(index).contains(number)) { inEveryList = false; break; } if (inEveryList) result.add(number); }
            return result;
        }

import java.util.*;

public class DemonstrateStreamSingleUseJava8 {

        }

        }

Java 8 – Complete Runnable Program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class CalculateSumUsingParallelStreamJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6);
            System.out.println(calculateSumUsingParallelStream(numbers));
        }

    private static int calculateSumUsingParallelStream(List<Integer> numbers) {
            return numbers.parallelStream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sum();
        }
}
Java 7 – Complete Runnable Equivalent
import java.util.*;

public class CalculateSumUsingParallelStreamJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6);
            System.out.println(calculateSumUsingParallelStream(numbers));
        }

    private static int calculateSumUsingParallelStream(List<Integer> numbers) {
            int sum = 0;
            for (Integer number : numbers) sum += number;
            return sum;
        }
}

Q225Stream API

Transform and Filter Objects with a Stream Pipeline

Filter employees by department and transform them into display names.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(k) result space
Sample input / test data
Employees: [Asha-IT, Ravi-HR, Neha-IT]; department: IT
Expected output
[Asha, Neha]
Java 8 – Complete Runnable Program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class TransformAndFilterObjectsJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            List<Employee> employees = Arrays.asList(new Employee("Asha", "IT"), new Employee("Ravi", "HR"), new Employee("Neha", "IT"));
            System.out.println(transformAndFilterEmployees(employees, "IT"));
        }

    private static List<String> transformAndFilterEmployees(List<Employee> employees, String department) {
            return employees.stream().filter(employee -> department.equals(employee.getDepartment())).map(Employee::getName).collect(Collectors.toList());
        }

    private static class Employee { private final String name; private final String department; Employee(String name, String department) { this.name = name; this.department = department; } String getName() { return name; } String getDepartment() { return department; } }
}
Java 7 – Complete Runnable Equivalent

public class TransformAndFilterObjectsJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            List<Employee> employees = Arrays.asList(new Employee("Asha", "IT"), new Employee("Ravi", "HR"), new Employee("Neha", "IT"));
            System.out.println(transformAndFilterEmployees(employees, "IT"));
        }

    private static List<String> transformAndFilterEmployees(List<Employee> employees, String department) {
            List<String> names = new ArrayList<String>();
            for (Employee employee : employees) if (department.equals(employee.getDepartment())) names.add(employee.getName());
            return names;
        }

    private static class Employee { private final String name; private final String department; Employee(String name, String department) { this.name = name; this.department = department; } String getName() { return name; } String getDepartment() { return department; } }

Q226Stream API

Use peek to Inspect a Stream Pipeline

Use peek() as a debugging aid to observe values as they pass through a pipeline before a terminal operation.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(k) result space
Sample input / test data
Numbers: [1, 2, 3]; keep values greater than 1
Expected output
Filtered result: [2, 3]; Values observed: [2, 3]
Java 8 – Complete Runnable Program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class InspectStreamPipelineWithPeekJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3);
            System.out.println(inspectStreamPipeline(numbers));
        }

    private static String inspectStreamPipeline(List<Integer> numbers) {
            List<Integer> observed = new ArrayList<Integer>();
            List<Integer> result = numbers.stream().filter(number -> number > 1).peek(observed::add).collect(Collectors.toList());
            return "Filtered result: " + result + "; Values observed: " + observed;
        }
}
Java 7 – Complete Runnable Equivalent
import java.util.*;

public class InspectStreamPipelineWithPeekJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
            List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3);
            System.out.println(inspectStreamPipeline(numbers));
        }

    private static String inspectStreamPipeline(List<Integer> numbers) {
            List<Integer> observed = new ArrayList<Integer>(); List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
            for (Integer number : numbers) if (number > 1) { observed.add(number); result.add(number); }
            return "Filtered result: " + result + "; Values observed: " + observed;
        }
}
Explanation, edge cases and interview follow-up

Interview follow-up: Why should peek() not be used as the primary mechanism for business side effects?

Complexity: O(n) time; O(k) result space

Convert key-value records into a Map. When a key occurs more than once, retain the entry with the highest value.

Complexity: O(n) expected time; O(k) space
Sample input / test data
[("A", 10), ("B", 7), ("A", 15)]
Expected output
{A=15, B=7}
Java 8 – complete program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class MergeDuplicateKeysJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Map.Entry<String, Integer>> entries = Arrays.asList(
            new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>("A", 10),
            new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>("B", 7),
            new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>("A", 15));

        Map<String, Integer> result = entries.stream().collect(
            Collectors.toMap(Map.Entry::getKey, Map.Entry::getValue,
                (oldValue, newValue) -> Math.max(oldValue, newValue),
                LinkedHashMap::new));

        System.out.println(result);
    }
}
Java 7-compatible equivalent – complete program
import java.util.*;

public class MergeDuplicateKeysJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Map.Entry<String, Integer>> entries = Arrays.asList(
            new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<String, Integer>("A", 10),
            new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<String, Integer>("B", 7),
            new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<String, Integer>("A", 15));

        Map<String, Integer> result = new LinkedHashMap<String, Integer>();
        for (Map.Entry<String, Integer> entry : entries) {
            Integer oldValue = result.get(entry.getKey());
            if (oldValue == null || entry.getValue() > oldValue) {
                result.put(entry.getKey(), entry.getValue());
            }
        }
        System.out.println(result);
    }
}
Interview notes and follow-up

Approach: Identify the core data structure or API operation, preserve the required ordering and define how duplicates, missing values and exceptional cases should behave.

Edge cases: Test empty input, one element, duplicate values and boundary conditions where applicable.

Interview follow-up: How would you change the merge policy to retain the latest value instead of the maximum?

Additional Interview-Critical Problems (Q424–Q425)

Q424Interview extension

Find employees earning above their department average

For each employee, calculate the average salary of their department and return employees earning above that average.

Complexity: O(n) expected time; O(d) space
Sample input / test data
Engineering: Ana 120, Ben 90; Sales: Kim 80, Lee 100
Expected output
[Ana, Lee]
Java 8 – complete program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class EmployeesAboveDepartmentAverageJava8 {
    static class Employee {
        String name, department; int salary;
        Employee(String n, String d, int s) { name=n; department=d; salary=s; }
        public String toString() { return name; }
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Employee> employees = Arrays.asList(
            new Employee("Ana","Engineering",120), new Employee("Ben","Engineering",90),
            new Employee("Kim","Sales",80), new Employee("Lee","Sales",100));
        Map<String, Double> averages = employees.stream().collect(
            Collectors.groupingBy(e -> e.department, Collectors.averagingInt(e -> e.salary)));
        List<Employee> result = employees.stream()
            .filter(e -> e.salary > averages.get(e.department))
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
        System.out.println(result);
    }
}
Java 7-compatible equivalent – complete program
import java.util.*;

public class EmployeesAboveDepartmentAverageJava7 {
    static class Employee {
        String name, department; int salary;
        Employee(String n, String d, int s) { name=n; department=d; salary=s; }
        public String toString() { return name; }
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Employee> employees = Arrays.asList(
            new Employee("Ana","Engineering",120), new Employee("Ben","Engineering",90),
            new Employee("Kim","Sales",80), new Employee("Lee","Sales",100));
        Map<String, Integer> totals = new HashMap<String, Integer>();
        Map<String, Integer> counts = new HashMap<String, Integer>();
        for (Employee e : employees) {
            totals.put(e.department, totals.containsKey(e.department) ? totals.get(e.department)+e.salary : e.salary);
            counts.put(e.department, counts.containsKey(e.department) ? counts.get(e.department)+1 : 1);
        }
        List<Employee> result = new ArrayList<Employee>();
        for (Employee e : employees) {
            double average = (double) totals.get(e.department) / counts.get(e.department);
            if (e.salary > average) result.add(e);
        }
        System.out.println(result);
    }
}
Interview notes and follow-up

Approach: Identify the core data structure or API operation, preserve the required ordering and define how duplicates, missing values and exceptional cases should behave.

Edge cases: Test empty input, one element, duplicate values and boundary conditions where applicable.

Interview follow-up: How would you include employees whose salary equals the department average?

Q425Interview extension

Find all highest-paid employees in each department

Return every employee tied for the maximum salary within their department.

Complexity: O(n) expected time; O(n) space
Sample input / test data
Engineering: Ana 120, Ben 120; Sales: Kim 100, Lee 90
Expected output
{Engineering=[Ana, Ben], Sales=[Kim]}
Java 8 – complete program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class HighestPaidEmployeesPerDepartmentJava8 {
    static class Employee {
        String name, department; int salary;
        Employee(String n,String d,int s){name=n;department=d;salary=s;}
        public String toString(){return name;}
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Employee> employees = Arrays.asList(
            new Employee("Ana","Engineering",120), new Employee("Ben","Engineering",120),
            new Employee("Kim","Sales",100), new Employee("Lee","Sales",90));
        Map<String,Integer> maxSalary = employees.stream().collect(
            Collectors.groupingBy(e -> e.department,
                Collectors.collectingAndThen(Collectors.maxBy(Comparator.comparingInt(e -> e.salary)),
                    optional -> optional.get().salary)));
        Map<String,List<Employee>> result = employees.stream()
            .filter(e -> e.salary == maxSalary.get(e.department))
            .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(e -> e.department, LinkedHashMap::new, Collectors.toList()));
        System.out.println(result);
    }
}

        public String toString(){return name;}
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Employee> employees = Arrays.asList(
            new Employee("Ana","Engineering",120), new Employee("Ben","Engineering",120),
            new Employee("Kim","Sales",100), new Employee("Lee","Sales",90));
        Map<String,Integer> maxSalary = new HashMap<String,Integer>();
        for(Employee e:employees) {
            Integer old=maxSalary.get(e.department);
            if(old==null || e.salary>old) maxSalary.put(e.department,e.salary);
        }
        Map<String,List<Employee>> result=new LinkedHashMap<String,List<Employee>>();
        for(Employee e:employees) if(e.salary==maxSalary.get(e.department)) {
            if(!result.containsKey(e.department)) result.put(e.department,new ArrayList<Employee>());
            result.get(e.department).add(e);
        }
        System.out.println(result);
    }
}

Q426Interview extension

Use a functional interface that can throw a checked exception

JAVA
Java 8 – complete program
import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class CheckedExceptionInLambdaJava8 {
    interface CheckedFunction<T, R> { R apply(T value) throws Exception; }
    static <T,R> R applySafely(T value, CheckedFunction<T,R> function) {
        try { return function.apply(value); }
        catch (Exception ex) { throw new IllegalStateException("Operation failed", ex); }
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String result = applySafely("java", value -> {
            if (value == null) throw new IOException("Input is null");
            return value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
        });
        System.out.println(result);
    }
}

Java 7-compatible equivalent – complete program
import java.util.*;

public class PrimitiveFunctionalInterfacesJava7 {
    interface IntPredicate { boolean test(int value); }
    interface IntUnaryOperator { int applyAsInt(int value); }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int[] values = {2, -1, 4};
        IntPredicate isPositive = new IntPredicate() {
            public boolean test(int value) { return value > 0; }
        };
        IntUnaryOperator square = new IntUnaryOperator() {
            public int applyAsInt(int value) { return value * value; }
        };
        List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
        for (int value : values) if (isPositive.test(value)) result.add(square.applyAsInt(value));
        System.out.println(result);
    }
}

Q428Interview extension

Remove duplicate objects using a derived business key

Keep the first employee for each email address, preserving encounter order.

Complexity: O(n) expected time; O(n) space
Sample input / test data
Ana(a@x), Ben(b@x), AnotherAna(a@x)
Expected output

Java 8 – complete program
import java.util.*;
import java.util.function.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class DistinctEmployeesByEmailJava8 {
    static class Employee {
        String name,email;
        Employee(String n,String e){name=n;email=e;}
        public String toString(){return name;}
    }
    static <T> Predicate<T> distinctByKey(Function<? super T,?> key) {
        Set<Object> seen = new HashSet<Object>();
        return value -> seen.add(key.apply(value));
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Employee> employees = Arrays.asList(
            new Employee("Ana","a@x"), new Employee("Ben","b@x"),
            new Employee("AnotherAna","a@x"));
        List<Employee> result = employees.stream()
            .filter(distinctByKey(e -> e.email)).collect(Collectors.toList());
        System.out.println(result);
    }
}

Q429Interview extension

Merge overlapping intervals

Merge all overlapping intervals and return the merged intervals in ascending order.

Complexity: O(n log n) time; O(n) space
Sample input / test data
[[1,3], [2,6], [8,10], [9,12]]
Expected output
[[1,6], [8,12]]
Java 8 – complete program
import java.util.*;

public class MergeOverlappingIntervalsJava8 {
    static class Interval {
        int start,end;
        Interval(int s,int e){start=s;end=e;}
        public String toString(){return "["+start+","+end+"]";}
    }
    static List<Interval> mergeIntervals(List<Interval> input) {
        List<Interval> sorted = new ArrayList<Interval>(input);
        sorted.sort(Comparator.comparingInt(i -> i.start));
        List<Interval> result = new ArrayList<Interval>();
        for(Interval current:sorted) {
            if(result.isEmpty() || result.get(result.size()-1).end < current.start)
                result.add(new Interval(current.start,current.end));
            else result.get(result.size()-1).end =
                Math.max(result.get(result.size()-1).end,current.end);
        }
        return result;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Interval> input=Arrays.asList(new Interval(1,3),new Interval(2,6),
            new Interval(8,10),new Interval(9,12));
        System.out.println(mergeIntervals(input));
    }
}
Java 7-compatible equivalent – complete program
import java.util.*;

public class MergeOverlappingIntervalsJava7 {
    static class Interval {
        int start,end;
        Interval(int s,int e){start=s;end=e;}
        public String toString(){return "["+start+","+end+"]";}
    }
    static List<Interval> mergeIntervals(List<Interval> input) {
        List<Interval> sorted = new ArrayList<Interval>(input);
        Collections.sort(sorted,new Comparator<Interval>() {
            public int compare(Interval a,Interval b) {
                return Integer.compare(a.start,b.start);
            }
        });
        List<Interval> result = new ArrayList<Interval>();
        for(Interval current:sorted) {
            if(result.isEmpty() || result.get(result.size()-1).end < current.start)
                result.add(new Interval(current.start,current.end));
            else result.get(result.size()-1).end =
                Math.max(result.get(result.size()-1).end,current.end);
        }
        return result;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<Interval> input=Arrays.asList(new Interval(1,3),new Interval(2,6),
            new Interval(8,10),new Interval(9,12));
        System.out.println(mergeIntervals(input));
    }
}
Interview notes and follow-up

Approach: Identify the core data structure or API operation, preserve the required ordering and define how duplicates, missing values and exceptional cases should behave.

Edge cases: Test empty input, one element, duplicate values and boundary conditions where applicable.

Q430Interview extension

Print a hollow right-angled triangle

Print a right-angled triangle with stars on the boundary and spaces inside.

Complexity: O(n²) time; O(n²) output space
Sample input / test data
rows = 5
Expected output
*
**
* *
*  *
*****
Java 8 – complete program
public class HollowRightTriangleJava8 {
    static String buildPattern(int rows) {
        StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder();
        for (int row=1; row<=rows; row++) {
            for (int col=1; col<=row; col++) {
                if (row==rows || col==1 || col==row) output.append('*');
                else output.append(' ');
            }
            if (row<rows) output.append(System.lineSeparator());
        }
        return output.toString();
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println(buildPattern(5));
    }
}

Q431Interview extension

Print a concentric square number pattern

For n = 3, print concentric number layers decreasing toward the center.

Complexity: O(n²) time; O(n²) output space
Sample input / test data
n = 3
Expected output
3 3 3 3 3
3 2 2 2 3
3 2 1 2 3
3 2 2 2 3
3 3 3 3 3
Java 8 – complete program
public class ConcentricSquarePatternJava8 {
    static String buildPattern(int n) {
        int size=2*n-1;
        StringBuilder output=new StringBuilder();
        for(int row=0;row<size;row++) {
            for(int col=0;col<size;col++) {
                int layer=Math.min(Math.min(row,col),Math.min(size-1-row,size-1-col));
                if(col>0) output.append(' ');
                output.append(n-layer);
            }
            if(row<size-1) output.append(System.lineSeparator());
        }
        return output.toString();
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println(buildPattern(3));
    }
}
Java 7-compatible equivalent – complete program

Q306DSA / Matrix

Q432Interview extension

Traverse a graph using breadth-first search

Perform BFS from a starting vertex in an undirected graph, visiting neighbors in insertion order.

Complexity: O(V + E) time; O(V) space
Sample input / test data
Edges: 0-1, 0-2, 1-3, 2-4; start = 0
Expected output
[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
Java 8 – complete program
import java.util.*;

public class BreadthFirstSearchJava8 {
    static List<Integer> breadthFirstSearch(Map<Integer,List<Integer>> graph,int start) {
        List<Integer> order=new ArrayList<Integer>();
        Set<Integer> visited=new LinkedHashSet<Integer>();
        Queue<Integer> queue=new ArrayDeque<Integer>();
        visited.add(start); queue.add(start);
        while(!queue.isEmpty()) {
            int vertex=queue.remove(); order.add(vertex);
            for(int neighbor:graph.get(vertex))
                if(visited.add(neighbor)) queue.add(neighbor);
        }
        return order;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Map<Integer,List<Integer>> graph=new LinkedHashMap<Integer,List<Integer>>();
        graph.put(0,Arrays.asList(1,2)); graph.put(1,Arrays.asList(0,3));
        graph.put(2,Arrays.asList(0,4)); graph.put(3,Arrays.asList(1));
        graph.put(4,Arrays.asList(2));
        System.out.println(breadthFirstSearch(graph,0));
    }
}

Q433Interview extension

Perform topological sorting using Kahn's algorithm

Return a valid topological ordering of a directed acyclic graph using indegrees and a queue.

Complexity: O(V + E) time; O(V + E) space
Sample input / test data
Edges: 5->2, 5->0, 4->0, 4->1, 2->3, 3->1
Expected output
[4, 5, 2, 0, 3, 1]
Java 8 – complete program
import java.util.*;

public class TopologicalSortJava8 {
    static List<Integer> topologicalSort(int vertices,int[][] edges) {
        List<List<Integer>> graph=new ArrayList<List<Integer>>();
        int[] indegree=new int[vertices];
        for(int i=0;i<vertices;i++) graph.add(new ArrayList<Integer>());
        for(int[] edge:edges) { graph.get(edge[0]).add(edge[1]); indegree[edge[1]]++; }
        Queue<Integer> queue=new ArrayDeque<Integer>();
        for(int i=0;i<vertices;i++) if(indegree[i]==0) queue.add(i);
        List<Integer> order=new ArrayList<Integer>();
        while(!queue.isEmpty()) {
            int current=queue.remove(); order.add(current);
            for(int next:graph.get(current)) if(--indegree[next]==0) queue.add(next);
        }
        if(order.size()!=vertices) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Graph contains a cycle");
        return order;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int[][] edges={{5,2},{5,0},{4,0},{4,1},{2,3},{3,1}};
        System.out.println(topologicalSort(6,edges));
    }
}

Q316Backtracking

Use the standard supporting Node/TreeNode model documented in the data-structures appendix.

Java 8 solution
void permute(int[] a,int start,List<List<Integer>> out){if(start==a.length){List<Integer> p=new ArrayList<Integer>();for(int x:a)p.add(x);out.add(p);return;}for(int i=start;i<a.length;i++){swap(a,start,i);permute(a,start+1,out);swap(a,start,i);}}
Java 7 equivalent

The Java 8 version expresses the transformation with Streams or functional interfaces where appropriate; the Java 7 version uses loops, collections and anonymous classes.

Q434Interview extension

Validate whether a binary tree is a binary search tree

Validate a BST using exclusive lower and upper bounds, not only parent-child comparisons.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(h) recursion space
Sample input / test data
Tree: 8, left 3, right 10, left-of-10 2
Expected output
false
Java 8 – complete program
public class ValidateBinarySearchTreeJava8 {
    static class Node { int value; Node left,right; Node(int v){value=v;} }
    static boolean isValidBst(Node node,long min,long max) {
        if(node==null) return true;
        if(node.value<=min || node.value>=max) return false;
        return isValidBst(node.left,min,node.value) &&
               isValidBst(node.right,node.value,max);
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Node root=new Node(8); root.left=new Node(3); root.right=new Node(10);
        root.right.left=new Node(2);
        System.out.println(isValidBst(root,Long.MIN_VALUE,Long.MAX_VALUE));
    }
}

Q435Interview extension

Find the lowest common ancestor in a binary search tree

Find the lowest common ancestor of two existing values in a binary search tree.

Complexity: O(h) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data
BST root 6; values 2 and 8
Expected output
6
Java 8 – complete program
public class LowestCommonAncestorBstJava8 {
    static class Node { int value; Node left,right; Node(int v){value=v;} }
    static Node findLca(Node root,int first,int second) {
        while(root!=null) {
            if(first<root.value && second<root.value) root=root.left;
            else if(first>root.value && second>root.value) root=root.right;
            else return root;
        }
        return null;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Node root=new Node(6); root.left=new Node(2); root.right=new Node(8);
        Node result=findLca(root,2,8);
        System.out.println(result==null ? "Not found" : result.value);
    }
}
Java 7-compatible equivalent – complete program
public class LowestCommonAncestorBstJava7 {
    static class Node { int value; Node left,right; Node(int v){value=v;} }
    static Node findLca(Node root,int first,int second) {
        while(root!=null) {
            if(first<root.value && second<root.value) root=root.left;
            else if(first>root.value && second>root.value) root=root.right;
            else return root;
        }
        return null;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Node root=new Node(6); root.left=new Node(2); root.right=new Node(8);
        Node result=findLca(root,2,8);
        System.out.println(result==null ? "Not found" : result.value);
    }
}
Interview notes and follow-up

Approach: Identify the core data structure or API operation, preserve the required ordering and define how duplicates, missing values and exceptional cases should behave.

Edge cases: Test empty input, one element, duplicate values and boundary conditions where applicable.

Interview follow-up: How would you solve LCA for a general binary tree?

Q319Concurrency

Implement bounded blocking queue using wait/notify

Implement the concurrency concept with safe interruption, synchronization and lifecycle handling.

Complexity: O(1) average queue operations; O(capacity) space
Sample input / test data
int capacity = 2;
List<Integer> valuesToPut = Arrays.asList(10, 20, 30);
// With capacity 2, put(30) waits until a consumer removes an item.

Java 8 solution
class BoundedQueue<E>{private final Queue<E> q=new LinkedList<E>();private final int cap;BoundedQueue(int c){if(c<=0)throw new IllegalArgumentException();cap=c;}public synchronized void put(E e)throws InterruptedException{while(q.size()==cap)wait();q.add(e);notifyAll();}public synchronized E take()throws InterruptedException{while(q.isEmpty())wait();E e=q.remove();notifyAll();return e;}}
Java 7 equivalent

The Java 8 version expresses the transformation with Streams or functional interfaces where appropriate; the Java 7 version uses loops, collections and anonymous classes.

Q320Concurrency

Implement Token Bucket Rate Limiter

Implement the concurrency concept with safe interruption, synchronization and lifecycle handling.

Complexity: O(1) time; O(1) space
Sample input / test data

long refillRatePerSecond = 2;
TokenBucket bucket = new TokenBucket(capacity, refillRatePerSecond);
int requestCount = 5;  // evaluate five calls to bucket.allow()
Expected output

Java 8 solution
class TokenBucket{private final long capacity,rate;private double tokens;private long last=System.nanoTime();TokenBucket(long c,long r){capacity=c;rate=r;tokens=c;}synchronized boolean allow(){long now=System.nanoTime();tokens=Math.min(capacity,tokens+(now-last)*rate/1_000_000_000.0);last=now;if(tokens>=1){tokens--;return true;}return false;}}
Java 7 equivalent
class TokenBucket{private final long capacity,rate;private double tokens;private long last=System.nanoTime();TokenBucket(long c,long r){capacity=c;rate=r;tokens=c;}synchronized boolean allow(){long now=System.nanoTime();tokens=Math.min(capacity,tokens+(now-last)*rate/1_000_000_000.0);last=now;if(tokens>=1){tokens--;return true;}return false;}}

Additional Interview-Critical Problems (Q436–Q437)

Q436Interview extension

Coordinate worker threads with CountDownLatch

Start multiple worker threads and let the main thread continue only after all workers finish.

Complexity: O(w) thread coordination; O(w) thread resources
Sample input / test data
3 worker threads
Expected output
Worker completion messages appear in any order; All workers completed is always printed last.
Java 8 – complete program
import java.util.concurrent.*;

public class CountDownLatchCoordinationJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        int workerCount=3;
        CountDownLatch latch=new CountDownLatch(workerCount);
        for(int i=1;i<=workerCount;i++) {
            final int workerId=i;
            new Thread(() -> {
                try { System.out.println("Worker "+workerId+" finished"); }
                finally { latch.countDown(); }
            }).start();
        }
        latch.await();
        System.out.println("All workers completed");
    }
}
Java 7-compatible equivalent – complete program
import java.util.concurrent.*;

public class CountDownLatchCoordinationJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        int workerCount=3;
        final CountDownLatch latch=new CountDownLatch(workerCount);
        for(int i=1;i<=workerCount;i++) {
            final int workerId=i;
            new Thread(new Runnable() {
                public void run() {
                    try { System.out.println("Worker "+workerId+" finished"); }
                    finally { latch.countDown(); }
                }
            }).start();
        }
        latch.await();
        System.out.println("All workers completed");
    }
}

Q437Interview extension

Limit concurrent access using Semaphore

Allow at most two worker threads to access a protected resource at the same time.

Complexity: O(w) task scheduling; concurrency bounded by permits
Sample input / test data
4 workers; semaphore permits = 2
Expected output
Worker resource-use messages appear in a scheduler-dependent order; Completed is printed last.
Java 8 – complete program
import java.util.concurrent.*;

public class SemaphoreConcurrencyLimitJava8 {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        final Semaphore semaphore=new Semaphore(2);
        ExecutorService pool=Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4);
        for(int i=1;i<=4;i++) {
            final int workerId=i;
            pool.submit(() -> {
                boolean acquired=false;
                try {
                    semaphore.acquire(); acquired=true;
                    System.out.println("Worker "+workerId+" using resource");
                } catch(InterruptedException ex) {
                    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                } finally {
                    if(acquired) semaphore.release();
                }
            });
        }
        pool.shutdown();
        pool.awaitTermination(5,TimeUnit.SECONDS);
        System.out.println("Completed");
    }
}
Java 7-compatible equivalent – complete program
import java.util.concurrent.*;

public class SemaphoreConcurrencyLimitJava7 {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        final Semaphore semaphore=new Semaphore(2);
        ExecutorService pool=Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4);
        for(int i=1;i<=4;i++) {
            final int workerId=i;
            pool.submit(new Runnable() {
                public void run() {
                    boolean acquired=false;
                    try {
                        semaphore.acquire(); acquired=true;
                        System.out.println("Worker "+workerId+" using resource");
                    } catch(InterruptedException ex) {
                        Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                    } finally {
                        if(acquired) semaphore.release();
                    }
                }
            });
        }
        pool.shutdown();
        pool.awaitTermination(5,TimeUnit.SECONDS);
        System.out.println("Completed");
    }
}

Chapter 13 – Java 8 Stream API: Deep-Dive Coding (32 questions)

Q322Stream

Create streams from collections, arrays, values and empty sources

Build streams from the main Java 8 source factories and collect their values.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(n) result space
Sample input / test data
List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3);
Integer[] array = {4, 5};
Expected output
collection=[1, 2, 3]; array=[4, 5]; values=[A, B]; emptyCount=0
Java 8 solution
List<Integer> fromCollection = numbers.stream().collect(Collectors.toList());
List<Integer> fromArray = Arrays.stream(array).collect(Collectors.toList());
List<String> fromValues = Stream.of("A", "B").collect(Collectors.toList());
long emptyCount = Stream.<String>empty().count();
Java 7 equivalent (imperative approach)
List<Integer> fromCollection = new ArrayList<Integer>(numbers);
List<Integer> fromArray = Arrays.asList(array);
List<String> fromValues = Arrays.asList("A", "B");
int emptyCount = 0;
Code explanation and edge cases

What the code demonstrates: Use Collection.stream(), Arrays.stream(), Stream.of() and Stream.empty() according to the source. An empty stream is useful when a method must return a stream but has no values.

Edge cases / interview checks: Arrays.asList(array) is backed by the array; Arrays.stream(array) streams its elements. A stream is consumed by a terminal operation.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(n) result space

Q323Stream

Use IntStream.range and rangeClosed correctly

Generate half-open and closed integer ranges and calculate a range sum.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(n) result space
Sample input / test data
int start = 1, end = 5;
Expected output
range=[1, 2, 3, 4]; rangeClosed=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; sum=15
Java 8 solution
List<Integer> range = IntStream.range(start, end).boxed().collect(Collectors.toList());
List<Integer> closed = IntStream.rangeClosed(start, end).boxed().collect(Collectors.toList());
int sum = IntStream.rangeClosed(start, end).sum();
Java 7 equivalent (imperative approach)
List<Integer> range = new ArrayList<Integer>();
for (int i=start; i<end; i++) range.add(i);
List<Integer> closed = new ArrayList<Integer>();
int sum = 0;
for (int i=start; i<=end; i++) { closed.add(i); sum += i; }
Code explanation and edge cases

What the code demonstrates: range excludes the upper bound; rangeClosed includes it. boxed() converts IntStream values to Integer objects when a List<Integer> is required.

Edge cases / interview checks: When start is greater than or equal to end, range produces an empty stream. Check integer overflow for large sums.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(n) result space

Q324Stream

Generate sequences with iterate and generate

Create a deterministic numeric sequence with iterate and a generated sequence with a stateful supplier.

Complexity: O(count) time; O(count) result space
Sample input / test data
int first = 1;
AtomicInteger counter = new AtomicInteger(0);
int count = 5;
Expected output
iterate=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; generate=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
Java 8 solution
List<Integer> iterate = Stream.iterate(first, n -> n + 1).limit(count).collect(Collectors.toList());
List<Integer> generate = Stream.generate(counter::incrementAndGet).limit(count).collect(Collectors.toList());
Java 7 equivalent (imperative approach)
List<Integer> iterate = new ArrayList<Integer>();
for (int i=0; i<count; i++) iterate.add(first+i);
List<Integer> generate = new ArrayList<Integer>();
for (int i=1; i<=count; i++) generate.add(i);
Code explanation and edge cases

What the code demonstrates: Both factories can produce unbounded streams, so limit() is used to make the pipeline finite. iterate derives each value from the previous one; generate calls a Supplier.

Edge cases / interview checks: A stateful supplier such as AtomicInteger is suitable for this deterministic demo. Do not assume generated values are reproducible when using random or external state.

Complexity: O(count) time; O(count) result space

Q325Stream

Observe lazy evaluation in a stream pipeline

Record when filter and map execute to see that intermediate operations run only during the terminal collect.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(k) result space
Sample input / test data
List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3);
Expected output
filter:1; filter:2; map:2; filter:3; result=[20]
Java 8 solution
List<Integer> result = numbers.stream()
    .filter(n -> { System.out.println("filter:" + n); return n % 2 == 0; })
    .map(n -> { System.out.println("map:" + n); return n * 10; })
    .collect(Collectors.toList());
Java 7 equivalent (imperative approach)
List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>();
for (Integer n : numbers) {
    System.out.println("filter:" + n);
    if (n % 2 == 0) { System.out.println("map:" + n); result.add(n * 10); }
}
Code explanation and edge cases

What the code demonstrates: Building the pipeline does not process elements. collect() triggers traversal. For each element, filter runs before map; rejected elements do not reach map.

Edge cases / interview checks: Do not use peek() or side effects as core business logic. The exact execution strategy can differ for parallel pipelines and some optimized operations.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(k) result space

Q326Stream

Chain filter, map, distinct and sorted operations

Keep positive values, square them, remove duplicate squares and sort the result.

Complexity: O(n log n) time; O(n) space
Sample input / test data
List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(-2, 1, 2, 3, 2, 0);
Expected output
[1, 4, 9]
Java 8 solution
List<Integer> result = numbers.stream()
    .filter(n -> n > 0)
    .map(n -> n * n)
    .distinct()
    .sorted()
    .collect(Collectors.toList());
Java 7 equivalent (imperative approach)
Set<Integer> unique = new TreeSet<Integer>();
for (Integer n : numbers) if (n > 0) unique.add(n * n);
List<Integer> result = new ArrayList<Integer>(unique);
Code explanation and edge cases

What the code demonstrates: filter removes values, map transforms values, distinct removes equal results, and sorted orders the remaining values. Intermediate operations can be chained in a readable pipeline.

Edge cases / interview checks: Integer overflow is possible when squaring large integers. Use long or mapToLong when the input range requires it.

Complexity: O(n log n) time; O(n) space

Q327Stream

Convert object streams to primitive streams

Calculate the sum and average of integer values without keeping boxed values throughout the numeric operation.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(1) auxiliary space
Sample input / test data
List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(10, 20, 30);
Expected output
sum=60; average=20.0
Java 8 solution
int sum = numbers.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sum();
OptionalDouble average = numbers.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).average();
Java 7 equivalent (imperative approach)
int sum = 0;
for (Integer n : numbers) sum += n;
double average = numbers.isEmpty() ? 0.0 : (double) sum / numbers.size();
Code explanation and edge cases

What the code demonstrates: mapToInt changes Stream<Integer> into IntStream. IntStream provides primitive operations such as sum(), average(), min(), max() and summaryStatistics().

Edge cases / interview checks: average() returns OptionalDouble because an empty stream has no average. Avoid dividing by zero or silently assuming a value exists.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(1) auxiliary space

Q328Stream

Box primitive stream values only when objects are required

Convert a primitive IntStream into a List<Integer> and convert a Stream<Integer> back to a primitive sum.

Complexity: O(n) time; O(n) boxed result space
Sample input / test data
int[] values = {2, 4, 6};
List<Integer> boxedValues;
Expected output
boxed=[2, 4, 6]; sum=12
Java 8 solution
List<Integer> boxedValues = Arrays.stream(values).boxed().collect(Collectors.toList());
int sum = boxedValues.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sum();
Java 7 equivalent (imperative approach)
List<Integer> boxedValues = new ArrayList<Integer>();
for (int value : values) boxedValues.add(value);
int sum = 0;
for (Integer value : boxedValues) sum += value;
Code explanation and edge cases

What the code demonstrates: boxed() adapts a primitive stream to an object stream. mapToInt() unboxes values back to an IntStream for primitive arithmetic.
